Postgraduate MSc Professional Experience option available Accounting and Finance Take your career to the next level. Develop your financial skills and know-how with our comprehensive Masters in Accounting and Finance. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Previous Section Course Overview Next Section Jump to a section Course overview Careers Teaching and modules Facilities Entry requirements Fees and funding Apply Apply now Book on a postgraduate open event MSc Professional Experience MSc Start date September 2027 January 2027 May 2027 Location Chelmsford Award MSc Duration 1 year full-time Course durations vary slightly: 12 months (September starts), or 15 months (January and May starts). The Professional Experience option takes 24 months (September starts), or 27 months (January starts). Professional Experience Start date September 2027 January 2027 Location Chelmsford Award MSc Duration 2 years with professional experience Course durations vary slightly: 12 months (September starts), or 15 months (January and May starts). The Professional Experience option takes 24 months (September starts), or 27 months (January starts). 1st in the region for postgraduates progressing into senior roles. Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 If you’re driven to succeed in the ever-changing, innovative world of accounting and finance, this is the course for you. At ARU in Chelmsford, you’ll gain an understanding of global financial markets and the complexity of the industry. You’ll learn the most up-to-date practices alongside classmates from around the world in dynamic seminars and our Bloomberg Financial Market Lab, where you can learn the trade in a safe, supportive space. Accredited by ACCA Our Accounting and Finance degree is accredited by ACCA, which means you’ll be exempted from the five Applied Knowledge and Skills papers of the ACCA qualification. Why ARU? Gain a thorough understanding of global financial markets Collaborate with classmates from around the world Develop your analytical and trading skills in our Bloomberg Financial Market Lab Build your network with our industry contacts and guest speakers Enhance your employability with our optional Professional Experience year Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers A Master’s in Accounting and Finance opens a wealth of doors, in the UK and internationally. Working on the more analytical side of finance, or in forensic accounting, are just a couple of paths you might consider. Graduation doesn’t have to be the end of your time with us. You could choose to continue your academic career with a research programme at ARU, such as our Business PhD - School of Economics, Finance and Law . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules Studying accounting and finance is about understanding the language of business. It equips you with the analytical skills to make sound financial decisions. Laura Muncey, Deputy Head of School Gain a thorough understanding of international accounting and markets. You’ll explore international accounting and international financial markets, focussing on investment analysis and portfolio management. You’ll also look at corporate finance and financial strategies of organisations in the capital, financial and operational markets. In addition, you’ll study tax in theory and practice, learning how to provide tax advice, solve issues, and conduct audits professionally. You’ll top off your Master’s with your Postgraduate Major Project. Supervised by one of our expert academics, you’ll use suitable research methods to propose solutions to one or more problems in a relevant area of your choice. What will I study? MSc Professional Experience MSc Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 International Financial Markets and Investment International Accounting Applied Corporate Finance and Financial Strategy UK Taxation and Auditing Postgraduate Major Project Module details Professional Experience You can choose to study with us over two years (full-time), and take Professional Experience modules in Year 2, with a Preparation for Professional Experience module in Year 1. Professional experience modules Professional Project * Professional Project 2 * Professional Work Placement * Professional Work Experience * Module details What are Professional Experience modules? Professional Experience modules are a great way to learn more about an industry. They take place in Year 2 of your course, with each module lasting approximately 12 weeks (or one trimester). You can choose which modules to take. Options include project work on campus, and industry placements. Our Placements Team is here to help you secure a placement. How is Accounting and Finance assessed? We’ll assess your progress in a number of ways, mainly through informal question and answer sessions. You can also expect individual and group presentations, management reports, exams, presentation or written analysis of case studies, and assignments. Our assessment strategy is linked closely to your employability. You'll develop skills that can be transferred to the professional environment such as teamwork, communication and presentation skills, and the ability to work under pressure. Who teaches Accounting and Finance at ARU? Read profiles of teaching and research staff on this course. Dr Lenka Krupová Senior Lecturer Dr Wei Kang Senior Lecturer in Accounting and Finance Facilities Enjoy a range of facilities designed to support your studies and career development. These include extensive library and IT resources, and careers support through our Employability Service . After you graduate, you’ll have lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . You can also access support, should you need it, with study skills, health and wellbeing, and more. Take a guided tour and meet our students . Postgraduate MSc Accounting and Financial Management Gain comprehensive understanding of the theoretical and practical aspects of accounting and finance at ARU London. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Previous Section Course Overview Next Section Jump to a section Course overview Careers Teaching and modules Facilities Entry requirements Fees and funding Apply Apply now MSc 2 years part-time MSc Start date September 2027 January 2027 May 2027 Location ARU London Award MSc Duration 1 year full-time 2 years part-time It's possible for UK students to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as MSc/MA students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example if the MSc/MA course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. Develop the skills, knowledge and competencies necessary to evaluate financial information, analyse financial statements, value companies and make informed decisions. You'll gain an understanding of the regulatory framework that governs accounting and finance practices and comply with relevant laws and regulations, and build your analytical, critical thinking, problem-solving and decision-making skills through real-world accounting and finance applications. You'll also learn how to think and act as a global citizen by taking ethical, social and environmental considerations into account. Careers Prepare for a range of careers in the accounting and finance industry. You'll graduate with the in-demand skills and knowledge required to make informed financial decisions in today's rapidly changing and complex business environment. Whether you decide to go into investment banking, risk management, financial analysis, or consultancy, you'll be able to apply key transferable skills such as critical thinking, problem-solving, communication, teamwork and leadership. Teaching and modules At ARU London, we understand that the financial function of an organisation is the foundation of a dynamic and resilient business model. Through practical projects, case studies, simulations and experiential learning activities, you'll gain hands-on experience across the accounting and finance spectrum. Our inclusive curriculum also offers you opportunities to develop your critical thinking, problem-solving, communication, teamwork and leadership skills, preparing you to meet challenges and contribute to organisational growth and success. You’ll complete your Master’s with a Postgraduate Major Project – a substantial research project focussed on a relevant topic that interests you. What will I study? MSc 2 years part-time MSc Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Postgraduate Study Skills, Research Methods, and Ethics Corporate Reporting, Budgeting and Control Corporate Finance and Valuations Taxation, Audit and Assurance Investment and Risk Management Postgraduate Major Project (Accounting and Finance) Module details 2 years part-time It's possible to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as MSc/MA students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example if the MSc/MA course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. How is Accounting and Financial Management assessed? We'll assess you through assignments, presentations, and examinations, as well as your Major Project, which involves detailed research, analysis and reporting of a finance related issue. Facilities As a student at ARU London you'll have access to: over 30 lecture theatres ranging in size from those that can accommodate up to 200 students in a theatre-style seating arrangement, to others that are perfect for highly interactive seminars two interconnected buildings with libraries containing core texts, wider reading materials, printers, and computer labs. There are also multiple study pods and booths for group work or personal study. You’ll be supported by: our Employability Service, helping you develop skills, knowledge, and experience through a range of extra-curricular sessions and career-focused support experienced wellbeing advisors and counsellors, offering assistance with mental, physical, medical, and/or learning conditions a mobile app giving you 24/7 access to learning resources, the e-library, and your timetable. Please enable JavaScript for "Fees Information" section to function. Entry requirements Standard entry requirements MSc 2 years part-time MSc Applicants must have: the equivalent of a UK first degree at 2:2 or above plus relevant experience previously been taught in English and have sufficient command of English to undertake postgraduate study, or have an IELTS (or equivalent) score of 6.5 or better. If you have completed a bachelors degree or an equivalent non-UK qualification and did not achieve our required grades for entry, but can demonstrate that your life/work skills would make you suitable, you should still consider applying. Our published entry requirements are a guide only and our decision will be based on our assessment of your overall suitability for the course. We treat everyone as an individual, which means we will look at your whole application, including any relevant work experience and personal circumstances, as well as your educational qualifications. Applicants studying for other qualifications should contact ARU London to discuss their circumstances. Please contact [email protected] for more information. Postgraduate MBA Agribusiness MBA Explore the business of food and how it’s produced, distributed and consumed. Study at ARU in Writtle and prepare for a career in innovation. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Previous Section Course Overview Next Section Jump to a section Course overview Careers Teaching and modules Facilities Entry requirements Fees and funding Apply Apply now Book on a postgraduate open event MBA 2 years part-time MBA Start date September 2027 January 2027 Location Writtle Award MBA Duration 1 year full-time Course durations vary slightly: 12 months (September starts), or 15 months (January starts). The part-time option takes two years. 2 years part-time It's possible to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as MBA students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example, if the MBA course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. 1st in the region for postgraduates progressing into senior roles. Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 As climate change, resource scarcity and global food insecurity challenge traditional systems, they also unlock vast opportunities for innovation, impact and growth. On this MBA, you’ll develop the systems-based approach, sustainability insight, and digital fluency to meet these challenges. At the same time, you’ll develop your management skills, with a focus on strategy, decision-making, and leading people through times of change that require them to reskill, upskill, and adapt. Why ARU? Learn how to build more resilient and sustainable food systems Explore regenerative business models and circular economy thinking Gain digital and leadership skills, and the know-how to drive change Apply your knowledge to real-world challenges through live projects and industry collaboration Study on a campus with a history of agricultural excellence Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers Prepare to take on leadership roles in a rapidly changing industry. You’ll graduate with critical skills in sustainability, circular economics and strategic management, opening doors to careers in agribusiness, food supply chains, policy and sustainability consulting. Through hands-on projects and guidance from industry experts, you’ll gain the confidence to drive innovation, improve productivity and support sustainable growth in food systems worldwide. What can you do with an Agribusiness degree? You'll be equipped for senior management, consultancy or policy-making roles within multinational food brands, agritech firms and environmental agencies. Graduation doesn't have to be the end of your time with us. You might decide to continue your academic career and join a research programme at ARU. Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. Where have previous Agribusiness graduates worked? Our graduates have gone on to strategic corporate roles within international commodity trading companies, agricultural infrastructure firms, supply chain logistics specialists and sustainable food consultancy practices. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules This MBA equips future agricultural leaders with the economic insight and agri-tech innovation skills to drive sustainable food systems. Dr Rob Gowers, Course Director Learn and apply professional skills as you explore sustainable food systems. You’ll focus on the efficient use of resources, postharvest practices and supply chain management to reduce waste and environmental impact. You’ll analyse food security challenges, global sustainability goals, and innovative strategies such as Controlled Environment Agriculture. You’ll also evaluate current food systems and propose resilient, context-specific solutions for the future of agri-food production and global food security. You’ll complete your MBA with your dissertation – a substantial research project on a relevant topic of your choice. What will I study? MBA 2 years part-time MBA Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Sustainable Global Business Management and Circular Economics (15 credits) Postharvest Systems Management (15 credits) Food Marketing and Value Chain Management (15 credits) Applied Research (Methods) for Managers (15 credits) Food Security and Sustainable Farm Management (15 credits) Strategic Management (15 credits) Controlled Environment Agriculture (15 credits) Leading Sustainable Change Strategies and Innovation in Food Systems (15 credits) Postgraduate Major Project (60 credits) Into ARU Module details 2 years part-time It's possible to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as MBA students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example, if the MBA course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. What are the teaching times? Currently, this course is taught in intensive, structured blocks on Tuesdays and Thursdays. How is Agribusiness assessed? You'll be assessed through a variety of methods, reflecting our focus on case studies, data and research. These include written research-style papers and reports for commercial enterprises, debates, discussions, presentations, time constrained exercises and group work. Who teaches Agribusiness at ARU? Read profiles of teaching and research staff on this course. Dr Robin Gowers Senior Lecturer Dr Kami Baghalian Senior Lecturer in Crop Production Dr Anya Perera Deputy Head of School Dr Christos Gerofotis Lecturer Facilities Enjoy a range of facilities designed to support your studies and career development. These include extensive library and IT resources, and careers support through our Employability Service . After you graduate, you’ll have lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . You can also access support, should you need it, with study skills, health and wellbeing, and more. Take a guided tour and meet our students . All fees are for guidance purposes only. Your offer letter will contain full details of credits and fees, or you can contact us if you'd like more information. Additional course costs Tuition fees cover core learning materials and access to our campus resources. Additional costs may include optional attendance at key industry networking events, such as the annual REAP Conference. Accommodation and travel for any external site visits are not included. Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 Discover how an understanding of animal behaviour can help address global conservation challenges. By combining behavioural ecology, conservation biology and emerging technologies, this course equips you with practical research, data analysis and science communication skills. You'll gain hands-on experience applying animal behavioural science to real-world conservation issues alongside expert academics and environmental partners. Hear from our staff and students about studying Animal Behaviour Applications for Conservation at ARU. Close full-screen gallery. Hear from our staff and students about studying Animal Behaviour Applications for Conservation at ARU. Why ARU? Develop your expertise in animal behaviour through fieldwork, laboratory sessions and conservation projects Build career-defining research, technical and analytical skills in behavioural and conservation practice Work collaboratively with zoological collections and animal welfare organisations on real-world environmental projects and Live Briefs Conduct your major research project with supervision from leading academics from our Centre for Ecology, Evolution and Environment Enhance your field skills with an optional short course in France hosted by the Mediterranean Ecology Research Observatory for Practical Skills Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers This course expanded my technical knowledge for research and conservation and exposed me to several career paths I'd never considered. Noel Ellis, Graduate Ecologist, MKA Ecology Prepare to apply your understanding of animal behaviour to global conservation challenges. This course nurtures specialist scientific knowledge alongside practical research, analytical and communication skills valued across the animal and conservation sector. Through projects, fieldwork, lab sessions and professional networking opportunities, you'll graduate ready for a range of careers in conservation, research and animal science. Graduation doesn't have to be the end of your time with us. You might decide to continue your academic career and join a research programme at ARU, such as our PhD Biology . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. What can you do with an Animal Behaviour Applications for Conservation degree? Our Graduates pursue careers across wildlife conservation, environmental management, conservation biology, zoological collections, conservation charities and government agencies. Typical roles include: Conservation biologist Behavioural researcher Ecological consultant Conservation project officer Zoo conservation and education officer Environmental educator/community work Attending the 2025 Student Conference on Conservation Science Animal Behaviour Applications for Conservation student Afrika shares her experiences of the 2025 Student Conference on Conservation Science (SCCS) in Cambridge. Where have previous Animal Behaviour Applications for Conservation graduates worked? Recent graduates have built successful careers across the conservation sector, taking on roles such as: Marine Biologist, Benthic Solutions Aquarist, Sea Life Chalk Streams Project Officer, Cambridge City Council Data and Research Officer, Mammal Society Marine Biologist Expedition Guide, Hurtigruten Expeditions Teacher, Niagara University Fisheries Officer, Brown & May Marine Head of Conservation, Research & License, Woburn Safari Park Animal Technician, Agenda Life Sciences How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules Our PGT courses provide an opportunity to gain experience in real-world research environments. Prof Claudia Wascher, Professor or Behavioural Biology Explore how animal behaviour research informs modern conservation practice. You'll learn from internationally recognised experts in behavioural ecology, conservation genetics, animal welfare and global change ecology. Through lectures, workshops, laboratory classes, fieldwork and independent study, you'll develop skills in wildlife monitoring, GIS, genetics and quantitative analysis. You'll apply your learning to real-world conservation challenges, tailor your studies through specialist options and field courses, and complete an independent research project aligned with your interests and career goals. Your work will be assessed in a range of ways to reflect the scope and aims of our course. These include written assignments such as scientific reports and essays, fieldwork, case studies, group work and presentations. Who teaches Animal Behaviour Applications for Conservation at ARU? Dr Çağlar Akçay Associate Professor Dr Paty Celis Lecturer Dr Jim Littlemore Senior Lecturer Professor Claudia Wascher Professor Professor Jacob C Dunn Professor of Evolutionary Biology Professor Anna Nekaris Professor of Ecology, Conservation and Environment Facilities Study in our state of the art £40m Science Centre in the heart of Cambridge. Postgraduate MSc Animal Welfare and Conservation Develop advanced knowledge of animal welfare, nutrition, genetics, behaviour and conservation. Study at ARU in Writtle and drive positive change for the natural world. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 On this course, you’ll gain the scientific knowledge and hands-on experience you need to tackle current conservation challenges and shape the future of animal welfare and conservation. Taking an advanced, interdisciplinary approach to the biological, ethical and ecological factors that shape animal wellbeing, you’ll learn how ethical practice, human-animal relationships, and behaviour change can be leveraged to protect animals and the environments they depend on for generations to come. Why ARU? Focus on both animal welfare and conservation Learn from highly qualified staff involved in conservation and welfare projects Build your skills on a rural campus, with conservation areas and a working farm Work with livestock, exotic and companion animals Benefit from our relationships with Colchester Zoo, Essex Wildlife Trust and more Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers My time at ARU Writtle gave me the confidence and skills needed to further my career in animal welfare research. Alice King, MSc Animal Welfare and Conservation graduate Prepare for an impactful career promoting biodiversity and animal wellbeing. As well as vital scientific knowledge, research skills, and hands-on experience, you’ll graduate with an understanding of policy and legislation, and how behaviour change and community engagement can make a real difference in education, advocacy and conservation programmes. Graduation doesn't have to be the end of your time with us. You might decide to continue your academic career and join a research programme at ARU. Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. What can you do with an Animal Welfare and Conservation degree? Graduates from this course are highly employable for management-level roles in welfare, conservation, and research across government, NGOs, zoos, rescue centres, and organisations like DEFRA, RSPCA, RSPB, Natural England, and NatureScot. Potential roles include: Senior government positions, e.g., DEFRA quarantine officers. Animal health inspector. Specialists in farm animal nutrition, pet food manufacturing, breeding, veterinary medicines and pharmaceuticals. Roles in animal welfare charities. Positions in zoos, safari parks, and animal rescue centres. Opportunities with independent wildlife and conservation agencies. Where have previous Animal Conservation and Welfare graduates worked? Graduates from this course have gone on to roles including: Ecologist at Cherryfield Ecology Ltd Animal Keeper at Longleat Production Manager at Dietex Sales Manager at Orffa Business Development Executive at Vet Vision AI Animal Welfare Officer at The Animal Rescue Charity (ARC) (Foxdells) How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules Shape the future of animal welfare and conservation through scientific knowledge, practical experience, and real-world impact. Dr Sife Chinkunya, Course Director Dive into animal welfare, behaviour, nutrition, genetics and conservation. You’ll learn how diet impacts welfare in domestic, farm and zoo species, and develop skills in welfare inspection and nutritional assessment while getting hands-on with molecular techniques like PCR and electrophoresis. You’ll explore ethics, human-animal relationships and behavioural science for real-world welfare and conservation solutions. You’ll also gain practical experience in habitat management and biodiversity assessment. You’ll complete your Master’s with a Major Project – a substantial research project focussed on a relevant topic of your choice. What will I study? Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 Thrive at the forefront of our rapidly-evolving scientific world. Gain an advanced understanding of the medical applications of bioscience, including bioinformatics, while developing the practical skills and analytical techniques needed for careers in research, healthcare or industrial settings. You'll learn in laboratories that mirror real-world laboratory environments, ensuring you’re immersed in an authentic, industry-relevant experience from day one. Accredited by the Royal Society of Biology This programme has been accredited by the Royal Society of Biology following an independent and rigorous assessment. Accredited degree programmes contain a solid academic foundation in biological knowledge and key skills, and prepare graduates to address the needs of employers. The accreditation criteria require evidence that graduates from accredited programmes meet defined sets of learning outcomes, including subject knowledge, technical ability and transferable skills. Course Director Dr Grisha Pirianov introduces our Master's courses in Advanced Biomedical Science, Applied Bioscience, Biotechnology, and Molecular Microbiology. Close full-screen gallery. Course Director Dr Grisha Pirianov introduces our Master's courses in Advanced Biomedical Science, Applied Bioscience, Biotechnology, and Molecular Microbiology. Why ARU? Study in Cambridge, one of the world's leading life sciences and biomedical innovation hubs Gain hands-on experience in specialist tissue culture and molecular laboratories, including a Category 2 lab Develop expertise in next-generation sequencing, bioinformatics and advanced molecular techniques Study on one of the UK's few Royal Society of Biology Master's-accredited bioscience programmes Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers Develop the critical skills required for careers across the life sciences sector. Areas you could work in include research, environmental science, biotechnology, food and pharmaceutical industries. Opportunities include roles in laboratory research, quality assurance, scientific consultancy and technical services, with the ability to apply biological knowledge to address real-world challenges in health, industry and sustainability. What can you do with an Applied Bioscience degree? You’ll be well-prepared to progress into a wide range of careers within the biosciences sector, including academic, clinical and industrial research, clinical trials, product development, manufacturing and quality assurance. Graduation doesn’t have to be the end of your time with us. You could choose to continue your academic career with a PhD programme at ARU, such as our MPhil/PhD Biomedical Science . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules Our course will enhance your knowledge, strengthen your practical and employability skills, and equip you for a successful professional career in the Cambridge industrial cluster. Dr Grisha Pirianov, Course Director Develop advanced skills in molecular cell biology, biomedical genetics, bioinformatics and specialised topics in medical diagnostics. On this course, you'll gain hands-on experience of molecular and cellular techniques used in applied bioscience, including DNA analysis, microbiology and cell culture, before conducting an independent research project that enables you to develop significant expertise in your chosen area. Throughout the course you’ll have opportunities to attend seminars or events with Cambridge’s many biotechnology companies, such as the Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute, the Biomedical Campus at Addenbrooke's Hospital and the Babraham Research Institute. What will I study? MSc Professional Experience 2 years part-time MSc Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Contemporary Medical Diagnostics (30 credits) Molecular Genetics and Bioinformatics (30 credits) Laboratory Techniques in Applied Bioscience (30 credits) Professional and Ethical Practice (15 credits) Research Methods and Preparation (15 credits) Masters Research Project (60 credits) Module details Professional Experience You can choose to study with us over two years (full-time), and take Professional Experience modules (2x project modules or 2x placement modules) in Year 2, with a Preparation for Professional Experience module in Year 1 . You'll also complete your Postgraduate Major Project (60 credits) in Year 2. Professional experience modules Professional Experience Biosciences Project 1 (60 credits) * Professional Experience Biosciences Project 2 (60 credits) * Professional Placement 1 (Life Sciences) (60 credits) * Professional Placement 2 (Life Sciences) (60 credits) * Module details 2 years part-time It's possible to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as MSc/MA students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example if the MSc/MA course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. What are Professional Experience modules? Professional Experience modules are a great way to learn more about an industry. They take place in Year 2 of your course, with each module lasting approximately 12 weeks (or one trimester). You can choose which modules to take. Options include project work on campus, and industry placements. Our Placements Team is here to help you secure a placement. How is Applied Bioscience assessed? We use a range of assessment methods to enable both you and the university to check your progress during your studies and then to ensure that you meet the required standards when you complete the course. Although they vary, our assessment strategies are all carefully designed to challenge you so that you expand your critical and analytical thinking as well as your problem-solving skills. The assessments will enable you to demonstrate that you can synthesise existing knowledge and accumulate new knowledge, and will evidence the development of your professional practice. Some examples of assessment include poster and oral presentations, essays and portfolios of evidence. In addition, you will undertake practicals in many of the modules, developing your technical laboratory skills. Who teaches Applied Bioscience at ARU? Read profiles of teaching and research staff on this course. Dr Grisha Pirianov Senior Lecturer Dr Clett Erridge Senior Lecturer Dr Hussein Al-Ali Senior Lecturer Professor Havovi Chichger Professor in Biomedical Science Facilities Enjoy a range of facilities designed to support your studies and career development. Our Science Centre features four floors of labs and teaching space, with facilities for specialist tissue culture and microbiology laboratories and a modern, 300-seat lecture theatre. You'll have extensive library and IT resources, and careers support through our Employability Service . After you graduate, you’ll have lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . You can also access support, should you need it, with study skills, health and wellbeing, and more. Take a guided tour and meet our students . Postgraduate MSc Applied Data Science (Conversion) Designed for graduates from any discipline, our MSc Applied Data Science (Conversion) will help you industry-ready data science and AI skills employers are looking for. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 Whether you're changing career or expanding your technical expertise, this conversion course in the heart of the Silicon Fen provides a practical pathway into modern data science and AI. You’ll gain hands-on experience in programming, statistics, machine learning, data visualisation, predictive analytics and generative AI through real-world datasets, and graduate with the analytical and technical skills sought by employers across healthcare, finance, business, technology and research. Why ARU? Launch your data science career – no computing or data-related degree required Study and explore career opportunities in Cambridge’s ‘Silicon Fen’, a global hub for tech innovation Build in-demand skills such as data mining, machine learning, statistical modelling and AI Apply your knowledge through hands-on projects using real-life datasets and industry-relevant projects Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers Your mentorship and belief in me have helped me learn and develop skills that I will carry with me for the rest of my career as I start my new role as a data analyst. Merin Mathew, MSc Applied Data Science (Conversion) graduate Gain in-demand skills applicable to a range of careers. This course equips you with highly marketable practical and industry-ready skills needed to thrive in today's data-driven world. You'll develop expertise in programming, data acquisition and cleaning, data visualisation, machine learning, predictive modelling, and artificial intelligence using industry-standard tools and techniques. You'll graduate well prepared for careers in data science, AI, business analytics, healthcare, finance, technology, and research. Graduation doesn't have to be the end of your time with us. You might decide to continue your academic career and join a research programme at ARU. Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. What can you do with an Applied Data Science (Conversion) degree? Organisations and industries increasingly rely on AI and data-driven decision making to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. You might pursue careers in data science, artificial intelligence, business analytics, healthcare analytics, financial technology, cyber security, environmental modelling, smart manufacturing and research. The combination of technical, analytical and communication skills also supports you to progress into leadership roles within data-driven organisations. Where have previous Applied Data Science (Conversion) graduates worked? Previous graduates from this course have gone on to a range of roles, including: Data Scientist at NHS Arden and GEM CSU Data Analyst at Hilbrix Data Scientist at Twinkl Educational Publishing Data and Insights Manager at Adam Smith Institute AI Research & Product Development at Pathway AI Consulting Research Assistant at ARU Data Quality and Insights Analyst at National Energy System Operator Senior Data Analyst at Pay.UK How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules There are many paths to becoming a data scientist. What matters is curiosity, commitment and a willingness to learn and explore. Dr Mahdi Maktabdar Oghaz, Course Leader Develop the knowledge and practical skills needed to become a confident data scientist, whatever your previous academic background. You'll begin by building strong foundations through Analytical Techniques and Programming with Python, before progressing to Principles of Data Mining and Machine Learning, where you'll develop predictive models and extract meaningful insights from real-world data. In Applied Data Analysis and Research Methodology, you'll learn to analyse complex datasets using industry-standard tools and apply robust research methods to data-driven investigations. The course culminates in the Data Analytics Major Project, where you'll independently apply the knowledge and skills gained throughout the programme to solve a real-world problem in a domain of your choice. What will I study? Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Analytical Techniques (30 credits) Programming with Python (30 credits) Principles of Data Mining and Machine Learning (30 credits) Applied Data Analysis and Research Methodology (30 credits) Data Analytics Major Project (60 credits) Module details How is Applied Data Science (Conversion) assessed? We'll assess you in several ways, including time-constrained assessments, coursework assignments and a Major Project (dissertation). Our module case studies and Major Project assess your ability to analyse situations, identify key issues, select, synthesise and apply techniques and skills, and evaluate the appropriateness of solutions when compared to industrial practice. Your dissertation will be based on a real-world scenario. Who teaches Applied Data Science (Conversion) at ARU? Read profiles of teaching and research staff on this course. Professor Silvia Cirstea Deputy Head of School Dr Imran Ahmed Senior Lecturer Dr Faraz Janan Senior Lecturer Dr Mahdi Maktabdar Oghaz Senior Lecturer Facilities Enjoy a range of facilities designed to support your studies and career development. In our dedicated computer labs, you’ll use industry-standard data science tools, including Python, machine learning frameworks and data visualisation software. You’ll develop practical skills in data analysis, AI and machine learning through hands-on projects using specialist computing facilities. In addition, you'll have access to our extensive library and IT resources, and careers support through our Employability Service . Postgraduate MA Applied Linguistics and TESOL January start available Apply now Book on a postgraduate open event Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Jump to a section Introduction Course options Key facts Teaching and assessment Entry requirements Fees and paying for university Facilities and showcase Lecturers Careers Introduction Advance your career in language teaching, or even take it international. Explore the latest linguistics theories and apply them to your classroom practice. What type of teaching is best? Alastair Douglas 60 second seminar Senior Lecturer Alastair discusses the methods and techniques used by language teachers. Already have an ARU degree? You may be eligible for our Alumni Scholarship for students starting postgraduate courses. Study our MA Applied Linguistics and TESOL (Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages) in Cambridge, a city famous for language teaching, and boost your career prospects with new critical and analytical skills. On this course you’ll improve your theoretical understanding of language learning, which will help you to develop your professional teaching skills. You’ll explore the latest theories in topics such as second language acquisition and classroom theory and practice, examining different methods of analysis. Your studies will be supported throughout by our research-active and industry-experienced academics, including DELTA-qualified professionals. And if you already have the Delta or Trinity TESOL Diploma, we will give you 60 credits towards your degree. If you study this course by distance learning, you will not need to attend any face-to-face sessions. Read more Teaching times 2025-26 (subject to change for 2026-27) Trimester 1: Compulsory module: Fridays 3-5pm; optional modules: Tuesdays 2-4pm, Tuesdays 6-8pm, Wednesdays 10am-1pm Trimester 2: Compulsory modules: Tuesdays 6-8pm; optional modules: Tuesdays 2-5pm, Thursdays 12-2pm As a Masters student at ARU, we’ll help you learn to carry out your own research and how to compile and analyse quantitative and qualitative data. You’ll be able to use the critical-evaluative skills you develop on your own research project at the end of the course, as well as in your future career. Studying Applied Linguistics and TESOL will give you the chance to take part in our research seminars and high-profile conferences. We’ll also help you make valuable contacts for your future through our links to language companies such as EF, Bell, and Studio, a group for heads of language schools. Whether you study full-time in Cambridge or part-time by distance learning, this postgraduate degree opens up opportunities for you to become part of the international academic and professional English Language teaching and language-learning community. The impact of our English Language and Literature research was judged as "world-leading" in the Research Excellence Framework 2021 (REF2021) . Course Leader: Alastair Douglas (Cambridge) and Amanda Bailey (distance learning) Course options Please enable JavaScript for "Course options" section to function. Course options Key facts Please enable JavaScript for "Key Facts" section to function. Looking for different course options? 60 second seminars Previous. Next. Hear about Owen's experience Studying at ARU Having taught in Japan for several years, Owen decided to improve his professional skills and take the opportunity to look more broadly at teaching. Take a guided tour and meet our students. Take a closer look Our Creative Showcase shines a spotlight on what makes ARU creative and cultural – our spaces, places and people. Find out more about our community, the difference we make, the stories we tell, and the things that inspire us. You can also explore the work of our graduating students in our digital graduate showcase. Lecturers Previous. Next. Graduation doesn’t have to be the end of your time with us. You could choose to continue your academic career with a research programme at ARU such as our PhD English Language and Linguistics or PhD English Language and Intercultural Communication . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. If you studied for the Postgraduate Certificate or Postgraduate Diploma initially, you can choose to complete further modules and top-up to a full Masters degree. Get a taste of our teaching and research, engage with live discussions and find out what it's like to study on a Humanities and Social Sciences course at ARU. var configOptions = {"HeroIntroduction":"","HeroImage":null,"CourseInfoDisclosureTitle":"Combining course options","CourseInfoDisclosure":"","StartDateDisclaimer":"","AdditionalInfoSectionTitle":"","AdditionalInfoSectionText":"","AdditionalInfoTitle":"","AdditionalInfo":"","StaffHeader":"","StaffRichText":[],"CourseOptions":[{"Duration":{"Name":"1 year full-time","Id":"0e006fc1-d6c6-476d-b58d-0f7542981c6e"},"StartDate":[{"Name":"September 2027","Id":"12ba467c-68e1-4784-9b56-3b8ccb7cca9f"}],"Location":[{"ShortName":"Cambridge","AstraLocationCode":"cam","DisplayOrder":1,"Id":"e44a5b31-f469-4e5b-93ad-f9219a73fe81"}],"Modules":[{"Title":"Year 1","CoreModuleSectionHeading":"Core modules","OptionModuleSectionHeading":"Optional modules","Summary":"

On this Masters course you’ll study second language learning as a core module. You’ll explore the major themes that have emerged from the research on the second-language acquisition process. We’ll encourage you to use your own language learning and teaching experience as you assess these approaches.

Alongside this you’ll explore modern classroom operations, and have the opportunity to observe teachers in practice. Meanwhile your Major Project is an opportunity to explore in detail a topic that reflects your particular interest.

There's also a range of optional modules. Select 30 credits (one module) from: Materials and Course Design; Language, Communication, Identity; Beyond Borders; Intercultural Consultancy Project. Select a further 30 credits (one module) from: Postgraduate Research Methods; Communication and Conflict; Teacher Development and Management.

Modules are subject to change and availability.

Assessment
You will show your understanding of the theoretical issues explored on the course and their practical application through various methods, including portfolios, classroom observation tasks and critical essays. At the end of the course, you will also research and complete a 15,000-word major project.

","CoreModules":[{"Title":"Major Project for Masters Stage","Description":"This module will support you in the preparation and submission of a Masters dissertation, allowing you to explore in-depth a particular topic that reflects your academic interest.","Code":"MOD000545","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"cd0b1b77-e95a-473c-b0db-d28caa707aa9"},{"Title":"Second Language Acquisition","Description":"You’ll focus on the major themes that have emerged from literature on second language learning over the last three decades. You’ll examine some of the research on the second-language acquisition process, look critically at reports of second-language research, and examine some of the theories which endeavour to interpret research evidence. You will be encouraged to use your own language learning and teaching experience to assess the relative merits of such materials. The module is taught through weekly seminars, offered in the early evening to accommodate those who are in part- or full-time employment. You may be asked to prepare or analyse material for presentation and discussion in class. Students taking part in distance delivery will work in small groups with support from the tutor by means of the Virtual Learning Environment, with progress monitored through formative tasks. Your assessment will be in the form of an extended written assignment to be submitted at the end of the module.","Code":"MOD000535","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"068507fa-af75-48af-9263-826d9204ffb9"},{"Title":"Language Teaching in Context: Theory, Practice, Reflection","Description":"In this module you'll develop a research-informed understanding of how English is learned and taught across a range of TESOL contexts, including young learners, ESP, and both face-to-face and online environments. You'll engage with current scholarship on key principles, approaches, and debates in the field, including Communicative Language Teaching, Global Englishes/EIL, and the implications of teaching in multilingual, multicultural settings. Your learning will also be practical: you are invited to analyse two live or recorded lessons, with particular attention to classroom management and its impact on learning. Alongside this, you'll examine principles and practices related to the learning and teaching of the four skills, grammar, vocabulary, and phonology, as well as the nature and value of feedback. You'll also explore contemporary developments in TESOL, including learner autonomy and the growing role of AI in lesson planning and classroom practice. By the end of the module, you'll be equipped to make principled, evidence-based decisions that support your development as an adaptive, reflective TESOL professional.","Code":"MOD000536","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"fc5aba79-345c-4b30-b79f-9a83ebb0785e"},{"Title":"Into ARU","Description":"Entering higher education is exciting; but it can also be a daunting experience. At ARU, we want all our students to make the most of the opportunities higher education provides, reach your potential, become lifelong learners and find fulfilling careers. However, we appreciate that the shift from secondary education, or a return to formal education is, in itself, quite a journey. This module is designed to ease that transition. You'll be enrolled on it as soon as you receive an offer from ARU so you can begin to learn about university life before your course starts. Through Into ARU, you'll explore a virtual land modelled around ARU values: Courage, Innovation, Community, Integrity, Responsibility, and Ambition. This innovative module is designed as a game, where you collect knowledge and complete mini tasks. You'll proceed at your own pace, though we you to have completed your Into ARU exploration by week 6. If for any reason you're unable to complete by that date, we'll signpost to existing services so that we can be confident that you are supported.","Code":"","HideMdfLink":true,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"fe875ffc-613a-4b26-98b2-b567ca8891ec"}],"OptionalModules":[{"Title":"Materials and Course Design","Description":"You will explore the factors involved in the design of language courses and teaching materials, reflecting on one possible process of course design. You will start with an analysis of the context in which the course will take place, the needs of the learners, and current theories of language and language learning. You will move on to consider how course content can be selected and ordered in a principled way, how assessment relates to course design, and how and when courses should be evaluated. Finally, you will consider the evaluation, adaptation and creation of course materials. The face-to-face seminars will be a combination of teacher input, student input and discussion, both in groups and whole class. Students taking part in distance delivery will work in a small group with support from the tutor by means of the Virtual Learning Environment, with progress monitored through formative tasks. The assessment will be in the form of a portfolio and will give you the opportunity to consider what particular syllabus might be relevant to your own current or future teaching context. The elements of the portfolio will relate to particular units of the module, and the portfolio can therefore be progressively built up as the course proceeds.","Code":"MOD000537","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"597a339c-2c19-4843-afda-08faa5731488"},{"Title":"Language, Communication, Identity","Description":"In this module, you will explore the interrelationships between language, culture and society, and identity. Starting by looking at the connection between language and the individual, we examine key concepts of identity and linguistic variation. The notion of ‘self’ and its relationship to language is being investigated in the context of different social and cultural dimensions, including gender, race and ethnicity. The second part of the module moves towards a discussion of language policy from several angles. Using a case-study approach, we explore policy-making, including national language policies and aspects of educational policy in which language play a key role. You are encouraged to critically reflect on how your own lived experience relates to the issues under consideration in the module.","Code":"MOD008999","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"e0669ae4-47dc-498b-ad18-f85b51219d1a"},{"Title":"Beyond Borders Intercultural Communication Welfare and Policy","Description":"This module takes an interdisciplinary approach to introducing key topics and ways of working in the social sciences. You'll look at the development of relations, communicative styles and values between individuals and groups of different cultural backgrounds and delve into comparative issues concerning social policy and social welfare in the international and intercultural context. You'll do this by exploring areas such as gender equality, social housing, education and immigration and wider social concepts such as identity, intersectionality and inequality. You'll work with case studies to exemplify these concepts. In this way, you'll develop the foundation for a deeper understanding and appreciation of fundamental topics in the social sciences. You'll also receive guidance on study at Master’s level and the module will guide you towards the academic research and writing skills needed to work independently at this level.","Code":"MOD010759","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"bbb89968-3e72-43f6-86a5-634020d297e9"},{"Title":"Intercultural Consultancy Project","Description":"Working with an external collaborative partner, you will negotiate a 12 week consultancy project that demonstrates and builds upon theoretical and practical skills you have acquired on your course. The module will enable you to work contextually within the framework of work-based learning by facilitating knowledge exchange between the student and their external partner. The project will respond to the opportunities and needs of the external partner as applied to the field of intercultural communications. You will critically engage with how this professional sector operates in context of the wider business environments and how this can be applied to your career development. This module supports you in the development of key skills required in contemporary intercultural work environments, such as face-to-face and asynchronous communications, collaborative and cooperative decision making or intra-team conflict resolution.","Code":"MOD008998","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"828f471c-8924-483e-b522-4be3447c71d2"},{"Title":"Postgraduate Research Methods","Description":"In this module you'll gain the research skills and techniques needed both to critically evaluate the literature you'll be using in your course and to put into practice in your own dissertation. We'll explore the methodologies and methods applied in contemporary social science research to enable you to select an appropriate range for your own needs. You'll have the opportunity to experiment with a variety of methods so that you'll fully understood them and be able to adapt them creatively for your own projects. The module will place research methods in a wider framework of social research strategies at a postgraduate level. We'll examine the research design options available to you at Masters level and explore thoroughly the issues involved in planning a research project and formulating research questions. With the aid of library expertise, you'll have access to and understand current tools for reviewing and researching existing literature. Particular attention will be paid to ethical principles and the politics of social research. A central part of the module will address the practicalities of employing both qualitative and quantitative methodologies. Computer-assisted analysis methods will be introduced.","Code":"MOD000825","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"5b02c3ba-c947-4e80-93fc-9a64099bcba0"},{"Title":"Communication and Conflict","Description":"On this module you'll explore historical and thematic approaches to reporting on conflict and also how communication functions in a crisis. You'll examine the reciprocal relationships between the military, governments and the media, including how the media can be used to legitimise conflict, and the changing role of social media in building consensus and protest, including the use of Twitter and Facebook to organise demonstrations and undermine the power of state-dominated discourses. You’ll also consider more traditional forms of communication, including censorship and propaganda, and whether the state is ever able to retain control of the narrative, as well as the role of the war reporter, and the way in which governments can utilise the independent media and how independent it really is. Other areas of exploration include consent, public interest, ethics and the representation of suffering, looking at whether the dominance of media in the debate in the West means that public interest in conflict is limited by the limitations of the media, and what this means for winning hearts and minds during insurgencies, military interventions and peacekeeping operations. Finally, you'll look at the way war and conflict is portrayed in fictional accounts and the underlying assumptions of such portrayals, and will examine conflicting discourses about war in post-conflict environments and the way the media can contribute to or hamper the process of post-conflict reconstruction. Themes throughout the module will include the question of who owns, defines and propagates the truth, and the implications of this in the context of conflict and war.","Code":"MOD003644","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"a956aeb6-6c48-423b-b081-fb889035e622"},{"Title":"Teacher Development and Management","Description":"In this module you will develop an understanding of the issues and practices concerned with developing and training teachers of English to speakers of other languages. You will examine current and recent research and explore the key concepts and practices in areas such as observing teachers and giving feedback, designing training programmes, leadership in academic management and professionalism within teaching. You will watch live or recorded lessons and develop ideas about what feedback you would give on the lessons to develop the teacher’s skills. You will reflect on your experience of working within teaching organisations.
