Through a structured curriculum with lectures, seminars, workshops, teamwork and independent studio practice, you'll explore different aspects of illustration such as its role and impact in social and changemaking projects; material expression; image and text relationships; and semiotics and narratology, as well as audience engagement; illustration, design and social research methods; critical analysis; and creative project management, which you will put to immediate use on the course as well as in your future career.

Modules are subject to change and availability. Some modules are shared to encourage cross-disciplinary exchange.

Assessment
You’ll show your progress through your self-directed visual projects, which will include extended written project proposals, developmental and final visual work, a reflective commentary, and an academic report of 3000 words. The Masters Project will allow you to build on all previous modules to design a visual project which shows mastery of your subject. We offer the guidance and structure to self-organise a degree show, which will show your work, but also evidence your project management abilities.

","CoreModules":[{"Title":"Visual Text","Description":"In this studio-based module, relationships between text and image, words, authorship, and the artist's voice are explored through a series of set and self-directed visual projects. Lectures and seminars will examine the role of text and typographic identity in the generation of meaning, and explore more complex and ambiguous text-image relationships. A large proportion of the teaching and learning activities will be focused around the development and resolution of individual student research projects, with group critiques and tutorials centred on developing visual practice. As with all our modules, self-directed study, and the ongoing development of visual work on a weekly basis outside of taught sessions, is a necessary part of this module.","Code":"MOD000228","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"9cca733d-a3e4-4946-85d6-998ab3747d21"},{"Title":"Image and Impact","Description":"In this investigative module you are asked to explore the key principles of the illustrated image, namely aesthetics, narration, semantics and rhetoric and how these shape the role of illustration as well as your personal visual language and approach. This is a practice-led research module. Supported by lectures and seminars where you will reflect on contemporary theory and practice in relation to visual language, narratology, material expression and visual rhetoric in single and serial visual work. You are expected to propose and resolve a self-contained project or projects. A large proportion of the teaching and learning activities will be focused around the development and resolution of individual student research projects, with group critiques and tutorials centred on developing visual practice. Self-directed study and the ongoing development of visual work on weekly basis outside of taught sessions is a necessary part of the module.","Code":"MOD009037","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"a533961a-fe9f-4e1a-abbe-6dc101b3fa2b"}],"OptionalModules":[],"Id":"ba98a2d3-e756-4fca-8d4e-9e78cec269b4","SelectedModule":false},{"Title":"Year 2","CoreModuleSectionHeading":"Core modules","OptionModuleSectionHeading":"","Summary":"

Through a structured curriculum with lectures, seminars, workshops, teamwork and independent studio practice, you'll explore different aspects of illustration such as its role and impact in social and changemaking projects; material expression; image and text relationships; and semiotics and narratology, as well as audience engagement; illustration, design and social research methods; critical analysis; and creative project management, which you will put to immediate use on the course as well as in your future career.

Modules are subject to change and availability. Some modules are shared to encourage cross-disciplinary exchange.

Assessment
You’ll show your progress through your self-directed visual projects, which will include extended written project proposals, developmental and final visual work, a reflective commentary, and an academic report of 3000 words. The Masters Project will allow you to build on all previous modules to design a visual project which shows mastery of your subject. We offer the guidance and structure to self-organise a degree show, which will show your work, but also evidence your project management abilities.

","CoreModules":[{"Title":"Design Methods and Contexts","Description":"In this cross-disciplinary module, you'll explore how design and creative methods and structures inherent to graphic design and illustration and those used in other design approaches, such as in social design, systems design, design narratives and speculative design can play an important role in enabling and driving innovation processes. You'll investigate these methods and approaches in practice and theory and contextualise your findings with discussions around issues of modern-day societal connectivity, audience participation and environmental impact. You'll explore how existing and created tools can be effective in addressing a wide range of issues, particularly within the context of complex social and environmental issues, typical within public-facing institutes, organisations and social enterprises. Alongside theoretical, ethical, and structural understanding, you'll engage with professional strategies such as creative project management, cocreation, feasibility studies, and presentation. This wide-ranging enquiry is designed to equip you with background knowledge and a ‘tool-kit’ of methods and strategies which will enable you to embark on a multi-disciplinary and collaborative projects within social settings. This is a research-led but equally practice-based module, where reading and lectures are developed through critical reading, assignments, seminars and workshops in which you test your finding and developments.","Code":"MOD009035","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"210505fc-2d1e-47f3-bd9f-6a42b5451dec"},{"Title":"Practice Through Partnership","Description":"In this module you will build on the knowledge and skills you have obtained in Design Methods and Contexts, and apply them to a live project in a real-world setting. In partnership with a mentor from an institutional, research, or governmental body, you will develop a creative proposal that seeks to make a social or environmental change. Working as a member of a cross-disciplinary team, you will test your ability to respond creatively and effectively to complex, change making briefs, as well as developing your organisational, team-working, and networking skills. As part of the team your tasks could include visual research, mapping, analysis, stakeholder interaction, socio-environmental and technical research, event organisation, and client negotiations - each a necessary aspect of developing real-world creative solutions and communications. Giving you first-hand experience of the diversity of issues around socio-environmental projects, this module will show how design methods can play a considerable, even essential role in the development of research, analysis, communication, and problem solving.","Code":"MOD009036","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"c7fd371e-bc33-4cf5-b2cc-851c23374f95"},{"Title":"Master's Project: Illustration","Description":"The Masters Project represents the culmination of your learning on the programme, giving you the opportunity to develop and resolve a major area of enquiry. This is a self-directed visual project negotiated with the staff team and peers. You'll need to negotiate, manage, co-ordinate and bring to successful conclusion a complex, practice-based project within your field of art, media or design. You'll start by formally presenting your research proposal to staff and peers, and will be expected to build on your previous modules to identify a complex area for investigation and enquiry, as well as research methods appropriate to the project. Following negotiation with staff, peers and, where appropriate, outside agencies, you'll then submit a written research proposal. Your project may involve external engagement alongside a personal exploration of themes and concepts in your specialist field. You'll need to show your ability to innovate, think strategically and be sensitive to changing cultural and social climates. You'll be assessed by portfolio (a body of work comprising a written project proposal, and developmental and final visual work) and a 1200-word reflective commentary. This commentary will specifically outline the methodological and ethical considerations relevant to your portfolio work, and evaluate your final visual work.","Code":"MOD006926","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"08ff6ef5-1fc9-4286-b242-b0f272de53b7"}],"OptionalModules":[],"Id":"1b0c9aca-bbe0-463a-8ea7-2aac88c49960","SelectedModule":false}],"UcasCode":"","SITSCode":"ACTTILBK","AstraCode":"P1047","ModeOfStudy":{"KisCode":"PartTime","ModeOfStudyCode":"PT","ExcludeFromCourseSummary":false,"Name":"Part-time","Id":"77ee6eb5-cef9-4099-87c0-3c2819c645cd"},"CoreOption":false,"FoundationOption":false,"PlacementOption":false,"ProfessionalExperienceOption":false,"PartTimeOption":false,"Extra1":false,"Extra2":false,"Status":null,"StartDateDisclaimer":null,"DegreeApprenticeship":false,"Award":null,"Qualification":null,"LocationOverride":null,"EntryRequirementYears":[{"Name":"2026","Id":"b0de6795-6e13-4745-98d9-c1515ee46eae"}],"EntryRequirementsInformation":[{"HeadingTitle":"Standard entry requirements","RichTextContent":[{"RichTextTitle":"","RichTextContent":"

Jump to a section Introduction Course options Key facts Teaching and assessment Entry requirements Fees and paying for university Facilities and showcase Lecturers Careers Introduction Learn how to communicate effectively in an intercultural workplace alongside students from all over the world, to prepare for a role in today’s global society. From teaching abroad to cultural research Intercultural Communication student Stephen talks about teaching overseas, furthering his understanding of communication and culture at ARU, and the success he's found as a lecturer, researcher and author since graduating. Stephen's story Already have an ARU degree? You may be eligible for our Alumni Scholarship for students starting postgraduate courses. On our MA Intercultural Communication, you’ll discover the importance of intercultural relationships both to the modern socio-economic climate – and to building a successful career within it. As part of our postgraduate community in Cambridge, you’ll work alongside students from all over the world, gaining an additional understanding of intercultural environments that will support your studies. Read more Teaching times 2025-26 (subject to change for 2026-27) 4-5 hours' lesson time per week As well as gaining business communication skills, you’ll explore language and cultural theory, and the research skills and techniques that you’ll need to both critically evaluate the literature on the course and put into practice in your own dissertation. You’ll also examine the development of relations, communicative styles and values between individuals and groups of different cultural backgrounds. By learning to use different methodological tools to understand language and communication, you’ll sharpen your analytical skills and gain the confidence to think independently about the interdisciplinary, and often multinational, challenges of the modern workplace. Seminars and guest lectures hosted by ARU’s Research Centre for Intercultural and Multilingual Studies will supplement your studies, and you’ll be supported throughout by our expert specialist lecturers. As a student on our MA Intercultural Communication you’ll join a course twice awarded the National Languages for Export award, given to organisations that promote the importance of understanding international culture and language. The impact of our English Language and Literature research was judged as "world-leading" in the Research Excellence Framework 2021 (REF2021) . Fees and Paying for University Facilities and showcase Outstanding student support Join our postgraduate student community and: benefit from award-winning learning facilities, including extensive library and IT resources learn from expert staff who will guide your research interests and career development access support, should you need it, with study skills, health and wellbeing, and more make the most of studying in the picturesque city of Cambridge , with its wealth of cultural connections and opportunities. Take a guided tour and meet our students. Take a closer look Our Creative Showcase shines a spotlight on what makes ARU creative and cultural – our spaces, places and people. Find out more about our community, the difference we make, the stories we tell, and the things that inspire us. You can also explore the work of our graduating students in our digital graduate showcase. Lecturers Bettina Beinhoff Associate Professor of Sociolinguistics Bettina Beinhoff's profile page [email protected] Follow Bettina on BlueSky Careers Our course will prepare you for a career in many roles relating to intercultural communication, such as consultancy, marketing, education, communication in specific fields (e.g. business and medicine), diplomacy, public services and international bodies like the UN and NGOs. It also offers you transferable skills and optional modules from other disciplines which help you to explore employment opportunities in the fields of international relations, sociology and research centres. Past graduates now enjoy careers in intercultural training, such as for Communicaid, or work with non-governmental organisations such as UNESCO and UNICEF. They also work in intercultural mediation in educational or social contexts, language teaching, translation/interpretation services, international property sales and business, education or embassy administration. After you graduate, you might also decide to continue your academic career with a research programme at ARU, such as our PhD English Language and Intercultural Communication . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. Apply now for MA Intercultural Communication Our course pages need JavaScript enabled for you to apply. Want to talk to someone? Your studies on this MA Intercultural Communication focus on the development of relations, communicative styles and values between individuals and groups of different cultural backgrounds. We also look at the research skills and techniques needed both to critically evaluate the literature you'll be using in your course and to put into practice in your Major Project (dissertation).

Your Major Project is an opportunity to explore in depth a topic that reflects your particular area of interest.

The course also features a number of optional modules which explore the sociology of identity and inequality; the relationships between language, culture, society, and identity; and how communication functions in a crisis situation. The Intercultural Consultancy Project module includes a 12-week project with an external collaborative partner.

Modules are subject to change and availability.

Assessment
You will demonstrate your progress on the course through written coursework (eg a 6,000-word essay) and short presentations in some modules. You will also complete a 15,000-word dissertation.

","CoreModules":[{"Title":"Beyond Borders Intercultural Communication Welfare and Policy","Description":"This module takes an interdisciplinary approach to introducing key topics and ways of working in the social sciences. You'll look at the development of relations, communicative styles and values between individuals and groups of different cultural backgrounds and delve into comparative issues concerning social policy and social welfare in the international and intercultural context. You'll do this by exploring areas such as gender equality, social housing, education and immigration and wider social concepts such as identity, intersectionality and inequality. You'll work with case studies to exemplify these concepts. In this way, you'll develop the foundation for a deeper understanding and appreciation of fundamental topics in the social sciences. You'll also receive guidance on study at Master’s level and the module will guide you towards the academic research and writing skills needed to work independently at this level.","Code":"MOD010759","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"bbb89968-3e72-43f6-86a5-634020d297e9"},{"Title":"Postgraduate Research Methods","Description":"In this module you'll gain the research skills and techniques needed both to critically evaluate the literature you'll be using in your course and to put into practice in your own dissertation. We'll explore the methodologies and methods applied in contemporary social science research to enable you to select an appropriate range for your own needs. You'll have the opportunity to experiment with a variety of methods so that you'll fully understood them and be able to adapt them creatively for your own projects. The module will place research methods in a wider framework of social research strategies at a postgraduate level. We'll examine the research design options available to you at Masters level and explore thoroughly the issues involved in planning a research project and formulating research questions. With the aid of library expertise, you'll have access to and understand current tools for reviewing and researching existing literature. Particular attention will be paid to ethical principles and the politics of social research. A central part of the module will address the practicalities of employing both qualitative and quantitative methodologies. Computer-assisted analysis methods will be introduced.","Code":"MOD000825","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"5b02c3ba-c947-4e80-93fc-9a64099bcba0"},{"Title":"Major Project for Masters Stage","Description":"This module will support you in the preparation and submission of a Masters dissertation, allowing you to explore in-depth a particular topic that reflects your academic interest.","Code":"MOD000545","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"cd0b1b77-e95a-473c-b0db-d28caa707aa9"}],"OptionalModules":[{"Title":"Communication and Conflict","Description":"On this module you'll explore historical and thematic approaches to reporting on conflict and also how communication functions in a crisis. You'll examine the reciprocal relationships between the military, governments and the media, including how the media can be used to legitimise conflict, and the changing role of social media in building consensus and protest, including the use of Twitter and Facebook to organise demonstrations and undermine the power of state-dominated discourses. You’ll also consider more traditional forms of communication, including censorship and propaganda, and whether the state is ever able to retain control of the narrative, as well as the role of the war reporter, and the way in which governments can utilise the independent media and how independent it really is. Other areas of exploration include consent, public interest, ethics and the representation of suffering, looking at whether the dominance of media in the debate in the West means that public interest in conflict is limited by the limitations of the media, and what this means for winning hearts and minds during insurgencies, military interventions and peacekeeping operations. Finally, you'll look at the way war and conflict is portrayed in fictional accounts and the underlying assumptions of such portrayals, and will examine conflicting discourses about war in post-conflict environments and the way the media can contribute to or hamper the process of post-conflict reconstruction. Themes throughout the module will include the question of who owns, defines and propagates the truth, and the implications of this in the context of conflict and war.","Code":"MOD003644","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"a956aeb6-6c48-423b-b081-fb889035e622"},{"Title":"Language, Communication, Identity","Description":"In this module, you will explore the interrelationships between language, culture and society, and identity. Starting by looking at the connection between language and the individual, we examine key concepts of identity and linguistic variation. The notion of ‘self’ and its relationship to language is being investigated in the context of different social and cultural dimensions, including gender, race and ethnicity. The second part of the module moves towards a discussion of language policy from several angles. Using a case-study approach, we explore policy-making, including national language policies and aspects of educational policy in which language play a key role. You are encouraged to critically reflect on how your own lived experience relates to the issues under consideration in the module.","Code":"MOD008999","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"e0669ae4-47dc-498b-ad18-f85b51219d1a"},{"Title":"Intercultural Consultancy Project","Description":"Working with an external collaborative partner, you will negotiate a 12 week consultancy project that demonstrates and builds upon theoretical and practical skills you have acquired on your course. The module will enable you to work contextually within the framework of work-based learning by facilitating knowledge exchange between the student and their external partner. The project will respond to the opportunities and needs of the external partner as applied to the field of intercultural communications. You will critically engage with how this professional sector operates in context of the wider business environments and how this can be applied to your career development. This module supports you in the development of key skills required in contemporary intercultural work environments, such as face-to-face and asynchronous communications, collaborative and cooperative decision making or intra-team conflict resolution.","Code":"MOD008998","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"828f471c-8924-483e-b522-4be3447c71d2"}],"Id":"399c0a9b-25a6-4c1f-87e4-143fdf069d82","SelectedModule":false}],"UcasCode":"","SITSCode":"","AstraCode":"P0174","ModeOfStudy":{"KisCode":"FullTime","ModeOfStudyCode":"FT","ExcludeFromCourseSummary":false,"Name":"Full-time","Id":"3188d331-b419-4c02-bf25-30c84b6fff3d"},"CoreOption":false,"FoundationOption":false,"PlacementOption":false,"ProfessionalExperienceOption":false,"PartTimeOption":false,"Extra1":false,"Extra2":false,"Status":null,"StartDateDisclaimer":null,"DegreeApprenticeship":false,"Award":null,"Qualification":null,"LocationOverride":null,"EntryRequirementYears":[{"Name":"2026","Id":"b0de6795-6e13-4745-98d9-c1515ee46eae"}],"EntryRequirementsInformation":[{"HeadingTitle":"Standard entry requirements","RichTextContent":[{"RichTextTitle":"","RichTextContent":"

Your studies on this MA Intercultural Communication focus on the development of relations, communicative styles and values between individuals and groups of different cultural backgrounds. We also look at the research skills and techniques needed both to critically evaluate the literature you'll be using in your course and to put into practice in your Major Project (dissertation). 

Modules are subject to change and availability.

Assessment
You will demonstrate your progress on the course through written coursework (eg a 6,000-word essay) and short presentations in some modules. You will also complete a 15,000-word dissertation.

","CoreModules":[{"Title":"Beyond Borders Intercultural Communication Welfare and Policy","Description":"This module takes an interdisciplinary approach to introducing key topics and ways of working in the social sciences. You'll look at the development of relations, communicative styles and values between individuals and groups of different cultural backgrounds and delve into comparative issues concerning social policy and social welfare in the international and intercultural context. You'll do this by exploring areas such as gender equality, social housing, education and immigration and wider social concepts such as identity, intersectionality and inequality. You'll work with case studies to exemplify these concepts. In this way, you'll develop the foundation for a deeper understanding and appreciation of fundamental topics in the social sciences. You'll also receive guidance on study at Master’s level and the module will guide you towards the academic research and writing skills needed to work independently at this level.","Code":"MOD010759","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"bbb89968-3e72-43f6-86a5-634020d297e9"},{"Title":"Postgraduate Research Methods","Description":"In this module you'll gain the research skills and techniques needed both to critically evaluate the literature you'll be using in your course and to put into practice in your own dissertation. We'll explore the methodologies and methods applied in contemporary social science research to enable you to select an appropriate range for your own needs. You'll have the opportunity to experiment with a variety of methods so that you'll fully understood them and be able to adapt them creatively for your own projects. The module will place research methods in a wider framework of social research strategies at a postgraduate level. We'll examine the research design options available to you at Masters level and explore thoroughly the issues involved in planning a research project and formulating research questions. With the aid of library expertise, you'll have access to and understand current tools for reviewing and researching existing literature. Particular attention will be paid to ethical principles and the politics of social research. A central part of the module will address the practicalities of employing both qualitative and quantitative methodologies. Computer-assisted analysis methods will be introduced.","Code":"MOD000825","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"5b02c3ba-c947-4e80-93fc-9a64099bcba0"}],"OptionalModules":[],"Id":"5bc6e83c-9d13-459b-ba52-e5d952b345ad","SelectedModule":false},{"Title":"Year 2","CoreModuleSectionHeading":"Core modules","OptionModuleSectionHeading":"Optional modules","Summary":"

The Intercultural Consultancy Project module includes a 12-week project with an external collaborative partner.

Modules are subject to change and availability.

Assessment
You will demonstrate your progress on the course through written coursework (eg a 6,000-word essay) and short presentations in some modules. You will also complete a 15,000-word dissertation.

","CoreModules":[{"Title":"Postgraduate Research Methods","Description":"In this module you'll gain the research skills and techniques needed both to critically evaluate the literature you'll be using in your course and to put into practice in your own dissertation. We'll explore the methodologies and methods applied in contemporary social science research to enable you to select an appropriate range for your own needs. You'll have the opportunity to experiment with a variety of methods so that you'll fully understood them and be able to adapt them creatively for your own projects. The module will place research methods in a wider framework of social research strategies at a postgraduate level. We'll examine the research design options available to you at Masters level and explore thoroughly the issues involved in planning a research project and formulating research questions. With the aid of library expertise, you'll have access to and understand current tools for reviewing and researching existing literature. Particular attention will be paid to ethical principles and the politics of social research. A central part of the module will address the practicalities of employing both qualitative and quantitative methodologies. You’ll experience a mixture of cultures, practices and experiences. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. The Professional Experience option takes 2 years, or 20 months for May starts. The May start for the Professional Experience option is only available in Chelmsford. Course content and modules remain the same. Professional Experience Start date September 2027 January 2027 May 2027 Location Cambridge Chelmsford Award MSc Duration 2 years with professional experience The course durations vary slightly: 12 months (September starts), 16 months (January starts) or 20 months (May starts). The Professional Experience option takes 2 years, or 20 months for May starts. The May start for the Professional Experience option is only available in Chelmsford. Course content and modules remain the same. 1st in the region for postgraduates progressing into senior roles. Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 Get ahead of the competition and carve your own career path at ARU studying business management. Studying a Masters in International Business is a great way to develop your career, increase your earning potential and study a subject you love. There’s the option to study our International Business course for two years and gain valuable experience with a choice of with a choice of professional experience modules, or to study abroad in Switzerland or the Netherlands for a semester, gain experience in international business operations, and graduate with a dual Masters degree. Why ARU? Build skills and experience in leadership, strategy and decision-making Cover topics including finance, supply chains, marketing and brand management Gain a global perspective on managing people and business operations Enhance your employability with our optional Professional Experience year Experience business in Switzerland or the Netherlands with an optional semester studying abroad Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers Studying International Business can open many doors, in the UK and globally. The course has been designed with your ambitions in mind. Whether you’re interested in business development, international supply chain management, brand management, marketing, HR or management consultancy, the opportunities are endless with an International Business course. What can you do with an International Business degree? Graduating from your International Business course doesn’t have to be the end of your time with us. You could choose to continue your academic career with a research programme at ARU, such as our Business PhD - School of Economics, Finance and Law . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules You’ll study six core modules that range from financial decision-making and leadership to supply chain strategy. Explore international marketing and brand management, looking at how brands appeal to consumers in different markets around the world. You’ll be able to make a real contribution to industry research through your dissertation. With supervision, you’ll focus on aspects of the course that interest you the most and explore them in depth. What will I study? MSc Professional Experience MSc Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Contemporary Issues in International Management Supply Chain Strategy and Practice Finance for Decision Making (15 credits) International Marketing and Brand Management Leadership and Change (15 credits) Postgraduate Major Project Module details Professional Experience You can choose to study with us over two years (full-time), and take Professional Experience modules in Year 2, with a Preparation for Professional Experience module in Year 1. Professional experience modules Preparation for Professional Experience Professional Project * Professional Project 2 * Professional Work Placement * Professional Work Experience * Module details What are Professional Experience modules? Professional Experience modules are a great way to learn more about an industry. They take place in Year 2 of your course, with each module lasting approximately 12 weeks (or one trimester). You can choose which modules to take. Options include project work on campus, and industry placements. Our Placements Team is here to help you secure a placement. How is International Business assessed? We’ll assess your progress through a range of written assignments, portfolios and presentations. You’ll have the option to carry out both group and individual work. Who teaches International Business at ARU? Read profiles of teaching and research staff on this course. Dr Emily Mace Deputy Head of School (Marketing, Entrepreneurship and Tourism) Dr Evans Akwasi Gyasi Deputy Head of School Facilities Enjoy a range of facilities designed to support your studies and career development. These include extensive library and IT resources, and careers support through our Employability Service . After you graduate, you’ll have lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . You can also access support, should you need it, with study skills, health and wellbeing, and more. Take a guided tour and meet our students . Previous Section Course Overview Next Section Jump to a section Course overview Careers Teaching and modules Facilities Entry requirements Fees and funding Apply Apply now Book on a postgraduate open event Start date September 2027 January 2027 May 2027 Location Peterborough Award MSc Duration 1 year full-time You can choose to start this course in September, January or May. Course durations may vary slightly and you can contact us for more information. Course content and modules remain the same. 1st in the region for postgraduates progressing into senior roles. Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 With a strong focus on entrepreneurship, ethics, and sustainability, you'll learn how to adapt business to suit new opportunities or combat challenges without having a detrimental impact on society or the planet. You'll also be supported to develop your own management style and reflect on your personal effectiveness. With four core modules covering global operations, business strategy, supply chain management, and international trading from a legal and financial perspective; and a final independent research-based consultancy project, you'll be fully equipped for a sustainable career in business and management. Develop your leadership capabilities and global perspective on our MSc International Business Management degree. Close full-screen gallery. Hear from your Course Leader Why ARU? Develop a global mindset to manage complex operations Focus on entrepreneurship, ethics, and sustainability Make strong professional connections Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers Employability is at the core of this course, which will equip you with a wide range of transferable skills. You’ll learn the key dimensions that underpin strategic decisions in dynamic environments. Many of the international business-related skills learned are increasingly important across a wide range of sectors and industries. We’ll help you realise your management potential by exposing you to real-life consultancy opportunities, where you can forge industry connections. What can you do with an International Business Management degree? Once you graduate, you will be prepared to enter a wide variety of business management roles such as (international) business development manager, sales manager, HR and recruitment manager, operations, and supply chain manager. Global entrepreneurship is a key thread within this course so you may also join a family business or develop your own enterprise. Graduation doesn’t have to be the end of your time with us. You could choose to continue your academic career with a PhD programme at ARU. Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules Gain a comprehensive understanding of the challenges and opportunities that shape international business strategy. Learn to drive decision making in globalised businesses in the context of international trade, legal systems, and financial constraints. You’ll also develop your knowledge around international trading and contract law, and how to resolve disputes. You’ll develop a global mindset to manage complex operations across national borders, and gain an understanding of service and manufacturing to help you build a blended, global approach to operations management. You’ll review a real-life problem for a client organisation and formulate managerial recommendations: the project will support you to become an independent learner who can raise meaningful questions from given evidence. What will I study? Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 International Business Strategy Trading, Contracts and Transactions Global Operations Management Sustainable Supply Chains & Logistics Consultancy Major Project Module details Facilities Enjoy a range of facilities designed to support your studies and career development. These include extensive library and IT resources, and careers support through our Employability Service . After you graduate, you’ll have lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . You can also access support, should you need it, with study skills, health and wellbeing, and more. Take a guided tour and meet our students . Postgraduate MSc International Hospitality and Tourism Management Gain the latest knowledge and skills you need to progress into senior management positions in international hospitality and tourism with ARU London. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Previous Section Course Overview Next Section Jump to a section Course overview Careers Teaching and modules Facilities Entry requirements Fees and funding Apply Apply now MSc 2 years part-time MSc Start date September 2027 January 2027 May 2027 Location ARU London Award MSc Duration 1 year full-time 2 years part-time It's possible for UK students to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as MSc/MA students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example if the MSc/MA course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. Hospitality and tourism are vital sectors for national economies, but also intrinsically vulnerable to external disruptions such as pandemics, war, and recessions. On this course, you'll develop management strategies that take account of contemporary issues and emergent crises in hospitality and tourism, with a focus on sustainability and ethics in alignment with growing consumer concerns. You'll additionally gain an international perspective on topics such as marketing, branding, digital platforms, and human resources. Careers Prepare to take the lead in international hospitality and tourism. You'll graduate with the high-level strategic skills required to head up major enterprises and navigate contemporary issues and crises in these sectors. This course has been developed in consultation with leading sector experts and applies the latest industry research, equipping you with the knowledge you need to take your career to the next level or advance to doctoral study. Teaching and modules Discover how you can make a difference in a pair of vital, yet vulnerable sectors. Through practical projects, case studies, simulations and experiential learning activities, you'll have plenty of opportunities to apply your new strategic and management skills to real-world hospitality and tourism scenarios. By studying core topics around marketing, branding, and the use of digital platforms, along with human capital management issues and the changing patterns of the available talent pool across national boundaries, you'll gain a comprehensive overview of the challenges faced across international leisure organisations. You’ll complete your Master’s with a Postgraduate Integrative Project – a substantial research project focussed on a relevant topic that interests you. What will I study? MSc 2 years part-time MSc Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Postgraduate Study Skills, Research Methods, and Ethics Contemporary Approaches to Emerging Issues in Hospitality and Tourism International Hospitality and Tourism Operations Management Cross-Cultural Leadership and Human Capital Management Strategic Design, Innovation and Entrepreneurship in Hospitality and Tourism Postgraduate Integrative Project Module details 2 years part-time It's possible to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as MSc/MA students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example if the MSc/MA course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. How is International Hospitality and Tourism Management assessed? We'll assess you through assignments, presentations, and examinations, as well as your Major Project, which involves detailed research, analysis and reporting of a hospitality and tourism related issue. Facilities As a student at ARU London you'll have access to: over 30 lecture theatres ranging in size from those that can accommodate up to 200 students in a theatre-style seating arrangement, to others that are perfect for highly interactive seminars two interconnected buildings with libraries containing core texts, wider reading materials, printers, and computer labs. There are also multiple study pods and booths for group work or personal study. You’ll be supported by: our Employability Service, helping you develop skills, knowledge, and experience through a range of extra-curricular sessions and career-focused support experienced wellbeing advisors and counsellors, offering assistance with mental, physical, medical, and/or learning conditions a mobile app giving you 24/7 access to learning resources, the e-library, and your timetable. Entry requirements Standard entry requirements MSc 2 years part-time MSc Applicants must have: the equivalent of a UK first degree at 2:2 or above plus relevant experience previously been taught in English and have sufficient command of English to undertake postgraduate study, or have an IELTS (or equivalent) score of 6.5 or better. If you have completed a bachelors degree or an equivalent non-UK qualification and did not achieve our required grades for entry, but can demonstrate that your life/work skills would make you suitable, you should still consider applying. Our published entry requirements are a guide only and our decision will be based on our assessment of your overall suitability for the course. We treat everyone as an individual, which means we will look at your whole application, including any relevant work experience and personal circumstances, as well as your educational qualifications. Use our finance guide for postgraduate students to learn more about postgraduate loans and other funding options. Scholarships We offer a £1,000 Postgraduate Entry Scholarship to new applicants at ARU London who achieved a first class honours degree from a university in the UK. We also have a Master's Scholarship Programme that runs through our three intakes. Successful applicants will receive 50% off their Master's degree fee. To apply, please write 750+ words on your previous degree, areas of interest in the field of business, and why you wish to study at a postgraduate level. If you graduated from any ARU campus with an undergraduate degree, we offer £2,000 off your entire course fee when you enrol as a postgraduate student at ARU London. Please note that only one scholarship can be applied per student. The scholarship with the highest value will be taken into consideration. You'll take the same modules as LLM students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example if the LLM course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. This course covers several core areas of international law. You'll develop legal research skills, strengthen your ability to critically analyse legal issues, and explore a wide range of specialist topics through real-world scenarios and case studies. Study in London – one of the world’s key legal and commercial centres – and benefit from guest speakers, networking opportunities, and visits to legal institutions. Careers Prepare to succeed in legal practice, policy, governance or further academic study. In today’s competitive jobs market, graduates need to stand out from the crowd to secure that all-important job after university. The academic rigour and practical focus offered by this degree will significantly enhance your employability. Our academic team includes lecturers with both academic expertise and practical legal experience, ensuring that your learning is current and relevant. Throughout your studies, you can take part in events and one-to-one sessions organised by our dedicated employability team. These are designed to support your career development and may include CV writing workshops, interview preparation, careers advice, and visits from prospective employers. Teaching and modules Gain an international perspective on key areas of law. You'll study six core modules on this LLM International Law degree, covering regulation of global trade, finance and investment; the protection of individual rights; and the peaceful resolution of international disputes. You’ll complete your Master’s with a Postgraduate Major Project – a substantial research project focussed on a relevant topic that interests you. What will I study? LLM 2 years part-time LLM Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Postgraduate Study Skills, Research Methods, and Ethics Postgraduate Major Project (Law) International Law: Problems and Processes International Law and the Rights of Individuals International Economic Law and Policy International Dispute Settlement Module details 2 years part-time It's possible for UK students to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as LLM students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example if the LLM course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. What are the teaching times? Full-time students study on campus two days per week (10am-5pm). Part-time students study on campus one day per week (10am-5pm). How is International Law assessed? We'll assess you through written coursework, oral presentations, online quizzes, in-class tests, practical projects, reflective work, and your Major Project. Facilities As a student at ARU London you'll have access to: over 30 lecture theatres ranging in size from those that can accommodate up to 200 students in a theatre-style seating arrangement, to others that are perfect for highly interactive seminars two interconnected buildings with libraries containing core texts, wider reading materials, printers, and computer labs. There are also multiple study pods and booths for group work or personal study. You’ll be supported by: our Employability Service, helping you develop skills, knowledge, and experience through a range of extra-curricular sessions and career-focused support experienced wellbeing advisors and counsellors, offering assistance with mental, physical, medical, and/or learning conditions a mobile app giving you 24/7 access to learning resources, the e-library, and your timetable. Entry requirements Standard entry requirements LLM 2 years part-time LLM Applicants must have: the equivalent of a UK first degree at 2:2 or above plus relevant experience previously been taught in English and have sufficient command of English to undertake postgraduate study, or have an IELTS (or equivalent) score of 6.5 or better. If you have completed a bachelors degree or an equivalent non-UK qualification and did not achieve our required grades for entry, but can demonstrate that your life/work skills would make you suitable, you should still consider applying. Our published entry requirements are a guide only and our decision will be based on our assessment of your overall suitability for the course. We treat everyone as an individual, which means we will look at your whole application, including any relevant work experience and personal circumstances, as well as your educational qualifications. We will ask for a deposit of £4,000 or a sponsorship letter Find out about paying your fees . Paying for university It’s important to decide how to fund your course before applying. Use our finance guide for postgraduate students to learn more about postgraduate loans and other funding options. Scholarships We offer a £1,000 Postgraduate Entry Scholarship to new applicants at ARU London who achieved a first class honours degree from a university in the UK. We also have a Master's Scholarship Programme that runs through our three intakes. Successful applicants will receive 50% off their Master's degree fee. To apply, please write 750+ words on your previous degree, areas of interest in the field of business, and why you wish to study at a postgraduate level. If you graduated from any ARU campus with an undergraduate degree, we offer £2,000 off your entire course fee when you enrol as a postgraduate student at ARU London. Please note that only one scholarship can be applied per student. The scholarship with the highest value will be taken into consideration. We’ll explore the digital landscape with consideration to the consumer and digital populations, online customer experience, paid and organic SEM, web development, social media and influencers, programmatic marketing, strategy and campaign planning, relationship development, and analytics. Postgraduate MSc International Project Management Learn how to consistently deliver results as a project manager. Study at ARU London, close to many project management delivery and consulting organisations’ headquarters. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Previous Section Course Overview Next Section Jump to a section Course overview Careers Teaching and modules Facilities Entry requirements Fees and funding Apply Apply now MSc 2 years part-time MSc Start date September 2027 January 2027 May 2027 Location ARU London Award MSc Duration 1 year full-time 2 years part-time It's possible for UK students to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as MSc/MA students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example if the MSc/MA course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. On this course, you'll explore project management in a range of contexts, including long-run public sector infrastructure projects and short-to-medium-term projects in private sector businesses, public sector organisations and not-for-profit organisations. Our comprehensive curriculum and hands-on approach will equip you with a sound knowledge of project management, preparing you for roles across a range of industries. Association for Project Management Our course is accredited by the Association for Project Management (APM), meaning you’ll have access to their resources, communities of learning, and communities of practice. Careers Graduate with in-demand skills and practical experience. Professional project managers are in significant demand in the UK and internationally. Career opportunities for exist in the public, private and voluntary-aided sectors. Some of our alumni have gone on to be project management professionals in a range of organisations including consultancy, construction and infrastructure, retail, IT, supply chain and logistics, real estate. Some are owners of start-up consultancies, while others have gone on to doctoral studies or careers in academia. Teaching and modules Develop your all-round knowledge of project management. We'll cover research, leadership, law, innovation, change management, and the global project management environment. We'll take a practical, rather than an overtly academic or theoretical approach, reflecting the requirement of project managers to deliver hard and measurable results. You’ll complete your Master’s with a Postgraduate Integrative Project – a substantial research project focussed on a relevant topic that interests you. What will I study? MSc 2 years part-time MSc Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Postgraduate Study Skills, Research Methods, and Ethics Principles of International Project Management Cross-Cultural Leadership and Human Capital Management Project Logistics and Delivery Management International Project Management Execution Postgraduate Integrative Project Module details 2 years part-time It's possible to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as MSc/MA students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example if the MSc/MA course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. How is International Project Management assessed? We'll assess you through assignments, presentations, and examinations, as well as your Major Project, which involves detailed research, analysis and reporting of a project management-related issue. Facilities As a student at ARU London you'll have access to: over 30 lecture theatres ranging in size from those that can accommodate up to 200 students in a theatre-style seating arrangement, to others that are perfect for highly interactive seminars two interconnected buildings with libraries containing core texts, wider reading materials, printers, and computer labs. There are also multiple study pods and booths for group work or personal study. You’ll be supported by: our Employability Service, helping you develop skills, knowledge, and experience through a range of extra-curricular sessions and career-focused support experienced wellbeing advisors and counsellors, offering assistance with mental, physical, medical, and/or learning conditions a mobile app giving you 24/7 access to learning resources, the e-library, and your timetable. If you have completed a bachelors degree or an equivalent non-UK qualification and did not achieve our required grades for entry, but can demonstrate that your life/work skills would make you suitable, you should still consider applying. We will ask for a deposit of £4,000 or a sponsorship letter Find out about paying your fees . Paying for university It’s important to decide how to fund your course before applying. Use our finance guide for postgraduate students to learn more about postgraduate loans and other funding options. Scholarships We offer a £1,000 Postgraduate Entry Scholarship to new applicants at ARU London who achieved a first class honours degree from a university in the UK. We also have a Master's Scholarship Programme that runs through our three intakes. Successful applicants will receive 50% off their Master's degree fee. To apply, please write 750+ words on your previous degree, areas of interest in the field of business, and why you wish to study at a postgraduate level. If you graduated from any ARU campus with an undergraduate degree, we offer £2,000 off your entire course fee when you enrol as a postgraduate student at ARU London. Please note that only one scholarship can be applied per student. The scholarship with the highest value will be taken into consideration. Jump to a section Introduction Course options Key facts Teaching and assessment Entry requirements Fees and paying for university Facilities Lecturers Careers Introduction Discover how international relations theory affects real-world events, and develop crucial skills like decision making and debating. With prestigious guest lecturers and visits to think tanks such as Chatham House, you’ll gain all the experience you need for a role in global politics. Hear more from our Course Leader Meet our Course Director Hear Course Director Dr Solava Ibrahim talk to current student Neha about her journey from working at Manchester and Cambridge universities to arriving at ARU in 2016. Already have an ARU degree? You may be eligible for our Alumni Scholarship for students starting postgraduate courses. Attend prestigious guest lecturers and visits to think tanks such as Chatham House Focus on your own areas of interest with optional modules including global risk society, war reporting, and terrorism Develop your decision making, planning and debating with interactive sessions, specific scenarios and briefs Read more about MA International Relations Teaching times 2025-26 (subject to change for 2026-27) Three contact hours a week per module, with a total of six hours direct contact per week This course will give you an understanding of how international relations theory is applied to real-world policy and strategy, and the practical problems involved in this. You’ll examine the theory and definition of the ‘state’ and relations between different states, and the roles of other institutions and organisations, like multinational companies and transnational crime organisations. All your studies will contain a strong vocational element, with a focus on how theory affects, and is affected, by real events on the ground. As well as this foundation in general international relations theory and practice, you’ll also have the chance to focus on your own areas of interest. Our optional modules will let you choose from subjects like the global risk society, policing and security, corruption and cross-border crime, war reporting, and terrorism. To develop your decision-making, planning and debating skills, you’ll take part in interactive sessions, respond to specific scenarios and briefs, and undertake critical analysis. You’ll also receive advanced instruction in research methods, a vital skill both for your studies and your future career. With a supporting team of lecturers who have academic and professional backgrounds in international relations, you can be sure you’re receiving the latest theory and careers advice. We offer a range of core and optional modules, with optional modules sometimes changing depending on staff availability.

You’ll demonstrate your progress through a combination of role-play scenarios, briefs, written reports, poster presentations, group projects, dissertation, longer essays, case studies, research proposal, short analyses of global events, short review papers, practical data gathering exercises, and short abstracts of core course readings.
