Postgraduate MBA Master of Business Administration MBA - International Develop your understanding of successful business strategy and executive leadership on a global scale. Study for an MBA at ARU London. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Previous Section Course Overview Next Section Jump to a section Course overview Careers Teaching and modules Facilities Entry requirements Fees and funding Apply Apply now MBA 2 years part-time MBA Start date September 2027 January 2027 May 2027 Location ARU London Award MBA Duration 1 year full-time 2 years part-time It's possible for UK students to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as MBA students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example, if the MBA course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. If you're a professional seeking to improve your management and leadership skills and broaden your theoretical knowledge of business and management, this course is for you. You'll acquire a deep knowledge of all key business functions and gain a greater appreciation of the significance of the interrelationship of functional areas to the overall success of a business in international, national and local markets. Reflecting today's highly-connected world, we'll focus on the specific challenges facing organisations that have global operations, or that transact business internationally. Careers Prepare to take your career to the next level. Designed in consultation with senior industry professionals, our MBA is designed to broaden your knowledge and expertise, fulfil employers’ requirements, and help you progress in your career. You'll expand your outlook and skills in leadership; strategic decision making; problem-solving; change management, creativity, innovation and entrepreneurship; finance; operations management; marketing; and human resource management. Throughout your studies, you’ll have access to tailored support from our Employability Service, designed to help you prepare for your career. This includes workshops on CV writing, interview techniques, and career planning, as well as guest talks. Alternatively, you might decide to continue your studies and progress to a DBA or PhD, and we can advise on these. Teaching and modules Expand your business knowledge and skills across the board. You’ll consider how technology has created new dynamics of unpredictable volatility, from business innovation to political/cultural change, requiring leaders to have international awareness and lead across cultural and ideological boundaries. We'll examine how leaders embrace positive disruption in the marketplace to remain competitive and relevant, and explore the management and improvement of simulated operations, detailing process design and control, production layout, performance and more. We’ll also study start-up, small, medium-sized, multinational, multi-divisional, multi-industry, multicultural enterprises, and the complexities of sustainable competitive advantages, along with the role played by HR management in the efficiency of organisations. You’ll complete your Master’s with a Postgraduate Integrative Project – a substantial research project focussed on a relevant topic that interests you. What will I study? MBA 2 years part-time MBA Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 International Finance and Operations Postgraduate Study Skills, Research Methods, and Ethics Principles of International Marketing Cross-Cultural Leadership and Human Capital Management Global Supply Chain Management Postgraduate Integrative Project Module details 2 years part-time It's possible for UK students to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as MBA students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example, if the MBA course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. How is Master of Business Administration International assessed? We’ll assess your progress through a variety of methods including coursework, group assignments, activity-based assignments and exams. You can expect to take part in ongoing problem-solving activities, projects and presentations. You’ll also be able to access support material through our virtual learning environment (VLE). Professional Experience Start date September 2027 January 2027 May 2027 Location Cambridge Award MBA Duration 2 years with professional experience Course durations vary slightly: 12 months (September starts), 16 months (January starts), or 20 months (May starts). The Professional Experience option takes 24 months (September and January starts), or 20 months (May starts). £4,000 You may be eligible for our MBA Scholarship, which offers a fee reduction of up to £4,000. See if you're eligible for our MBA Scholarship If you’ve already immersed yourself in industry and want to sharpen your management and entrepreneurial skills, this MBA is for you. As well as gaining a rounded knowledge of different functions of business including marketing, human resources, and finance, you’ll take a global perspective by collaborating with classmates from around the world. Through practical, real-world assignments, you’ll develop as a communicator, critical analyst, decision-maker, and innovator. Study with us in Cambridge, or explore our distance learning option or our Double Master MIR+MBA with Geneva School of International Diplomacy & International Relations . Chartered Management Institute As an MBA student at ARU, you’ll bolster your advanced management training with Level 7 CMI accreditation, thanks to our partnership with the Chartered Management Institute (CMI). This qualification gives you a considerable competitive advantage and offers an effective route to career progression. Why ARU? Develop as an innovative and entrepreneurial leader Gain skills and experience in communication, critical analysis and decision-making Achieve Level 7 Chartered Management Institute accreditation and stand out from the crowd Build your network with our industry contacts and guest speakers Collaborate with classmates from around the world Enhance your employability with our optional Professional Experience year Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers Equip yourself with a prestigious management qualification. On our MBA, you’ll gain management and entrepreneurial abilities to succeed in a range of business fields. When you graduate, you’ll be confident about entering the international business market and finding a senior role in a corporation or taking the first steps towards self-employment. Graduation doesn’t have to be the end of your time with us. You could choose to continue your academic career with our Business PhD – School of Management . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules Gain an all-round understanding of business and entrepreneurship. You’ll study the main themes and principles of marketing and HR, their application in a variety of business contexts, and the challenges these functions can face. You’ll practise using strategic and financial analysis techniques to make informed management decisions and drive performance. You’ll also have the opportunity to deepen your knowledge of leadership, entrepreneurship and innovation, economics, or international business law with our optional modules. You’ll complete your MBA with a Postgraduate Major Project – a substantial research project on a relevant topic of your choice. What will I study? MBA Professional Experience MBA Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Principles of Marketing Management (30 credits) Organisational Psychology in a Social Context (30 credits) Management and Strategy (15 credits) Finance for Decision Making (15 credits) Entrepreneurial Action - PG Major Project (60 credits) Into ARU Leadership and Change (15 credits) * Innovation and Entrepreneurship (15 credits) * Economics and Behaviour (15 credits) * Introduction to Comparative Law (15 credits) * Module details Professional Experience You can choose to study with us over two years (full-time), and take Professional Experience modules in Year 2, with a Preparation for Professional Experience module in Year 1. Professional experience modules Consultancy Project * Business Simulation * Professional Work Experience Placement * Module details What are Professional Experience modules? Professional Experience modules are a great way to learn more about an industry. They take place in Year 2 of your course, with each module lasting approximately 12 weeks (or one trimester). You can choose which modules to take. Options include project work on campus, and industry placements. Our Placements Team is here to help you secure a placement. How is Master of Business Administration assessed? We place a strong emphasis on practical and professional skills. You’ll be assessed on work-based assignments, research projects, syndicate work and group presentations. Who teaches Master of Business Administration at ARU? Read profiles of teaching and research staff on this course. Postgraduate MPH Master of Public Health Prepare for an impactful career focused on improving health and wellbeing at a population level. Study for a Master's at ARU London. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Previous Section Course Overview Next Section Jump to a section Course overview Careers Teaching and modules Facilities Entry requirements Fees and funding Apply Apply now MPH 2 years part-time MPH Start date September 2027 January 2027 May 2027 Location ARU London Award MPH Duration 1 year full-time 2 years part-time It's possible to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as MPH students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example, if the MPH course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. Focussing on core areas of health protection, health improvement, and service development, on this course you'll explore how social, economic, and environmental factors influence health outcomes. We'll cover essential topics such as population health, health protection, and governance, and you’ll gain essential skills in research, leadership, critical thinking, and communication while exploring public health challenges through applied learning and real-world case studies. Careers Prepare for roles in local, national, and international public health organisations. Career opportunities for Master of Public Health graduates span the NHS, local authorities, NGOs, international bodies like the WHO, and policy think tanks. You might become a public health analyst, health promotion specialist, policy advisor, or global health consultant, or pursue academic research or doctoral study. You'll build transferable skills in research, communication, and strategic thinking. We offer dedicated career support services such as CV workshops, interview coaching, and an Enterprise Hub , which provides expert guidance for start-ups and consultancy work. Teaching and modules Develop your all-round public health knowledge and skills. On this course, you'll discover the most effective ways to make a difference in health protection, health improvement, and service development. You'll explore public health challenges through applied learning and real-world case studies, enabling you to practise skills you'll use in the workplace as a public health practitioner. You’ll complete your Master’s with a Postgraduate Major Project – a substantial research project focussed on a significant public health topic that interests you. What will I study? MPH 2 years part-time MPH Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Postgraduate Study Skills, Research Methods, and Ethics Determinants of Population Health Health Protection Finance and Governance in Health and Social Care Population Healthcare and Health Improvement Postgraduate Major Project (Healthcare) Module details 2 years part-time It's possible to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as MPH students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example, if the MPH course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. How is Master of Public Health assessed? You’ll be assessed through a combination of written assignments, presentations, and practical tasks, designed to reflect real-world public health scenarios. The course culminates in a major project or dissertation, where you’ll research, analyse, and report on a significant public health issue of your choice, allowing you to apply your learning to a real or simulated setting. Facilities As a student at ARU London you'll have access to: over 30 lecture theatres ranging in size from those that can accommodate up to 200 students in a theatre-style seating arrangement, to others that are perfect for highly interactive seminars two interconnected buildings with libraries containing core texts, wider reading materials, printers, and computer labs. There are also multiple study pods and booths for group work or personal study. You’ll be supported by: our Employability Service, helping you develop skills, knowledge, and experience through a range of extra-curricular sessions and career-focused support experienced wellbeing advisors and counsellors, offering assistance with mental, physical, medical, and/or learning conditions a mobile app giving you 24/7 access to learning resources, the e-library, and your timetable. Please enable JavaScript for "Fees Information" section to function. Entry requirements Standard entry requirements MPH 2 years part-time MPH UK qualifications Applicants must have: the equivalent of a UK first degree at 2:2 or above plus relevant experience previously been taught in English and have sufficient command of English to undertake postgraduate study, or have an IELTS (or equivalent) score of 6.5 or better. If you have completed a bachelors degree or an equivalent non-UK qualification and did not achieve our required grades for entry, but can demonstrate that your life/work skills would make you suitable, you should still consider applying. Our published entry requirements are a guide only and our decision will be based on our assessment of your overall suitability for the course. We treat everyone as an individual, which means we will look at your whole application, including any relevant work experience and personal circumstances, as well as your educational qualifications. Applicants studying for other qualifications should contact ARU London to discuss their circumstances. Please contact [email protected] for more information. If you have completed a bachelors degree or an equivalent non-UK qualification and did not achieve our required grades for entry, but can demonstrate that your life/work skills would make you suitable, you should still consider applying. Use our finance guide for postgraduate students to learn more about postgraduate loans and other funding options. Scholarships We offer a £1,000 Postgraduate Entry Scholarship to new applicants at ARU London who achieved a first class honours degree from a university in the UK. We also have a Master's Scholarship Programme that runs through our three intakes. Successful applicants will receive 50% off their Master's degree fee. To apply, please write 750+ words on your previous degree, areas of interest in the field of business, and why you wish to study at a postgraduate level. If you graduated from any ARU campus with an undergraduate degree, we offer £2,000 off your entire course fee when you enrol as a postgraduate student at ARU London. Please note that only one scholarship can be applied per student. The scholarship with the highest value will be taken into consideration. Postgraduate MSc Professional Experience option available Mechanical Engineering Master advanced mechanical engineering. Innovate, design and solve real-world engineering challenges on our IMechE-accredited MSc at ARU in Chelmsford. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. You'll take the same modules as MSc/MA students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example if the MSc/MA course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. 1st in the region for postgraduates progressing into senior roles. Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 Mechanical engineers who combine creativity with rigorous technical expertise are in demand across industry. On this Mechanical Engineering MSc, you’ll develop advanced design, analysis and manufacturing skills in specially equipped engineering laboratories. Explore modern materials and technologies, tackle complex engineering challenges and develop the confidence to innovate. If you hold a CEng-accredited bachelor’s degree, this MSc can contribute towards the educational requirements for Chartered Engineer registration. Institution of Mechanical Engineers Our Mechanical Engineering MSc is accredited by the Institute of Mechanical Engineers (IMechE). Provided you meet certain conditions, upon graduation you'll be able to satisfy the educational base for CEng registration. Why ARU? Work towards the educational base for Chartered Engineer registration Gain hands-on experience in specialist engineering laboratories, 3D printing studio and workshop Develop expertise in areas including robotics and mechatronics, product design and manufacture, sustainability, and engineering management Learn from expert staff with a range of industrial and academic backgrounds Choose our Professional Experience option to gain work experience and strengthen your employability Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers The course provided me with the technical depth, research experience, and industry connections that directly shaped my career as a Design Engineer. Soroush Parsa, MSc Mechanical Engineering graduate Take your mechanical engineering career further with advanced technical, analytical and problem-solving skills. This MSc can prepare you for roles across automotive, aerospace, marine engineering, consultancy and other technology-driven industries. Through guest lectures, site visits and networking opportunities, you’ll gain insights from industry and build valuable professional connections while developing the expertise to tackle complex engineering challenges. What can I do with an MSc Mechanical Engineering? Some of the careers that your Mechanical Engineering MSc could lead to include: Aeronautical engineering Automation and mechatronics Automotive engineering Control and AI (artificial intelligence) Mechatronics and robotics Process control and automation Graduation doesn’t have to be the end of your time with us. You could choose to continue your academic career on a postgraduate research programme, such as our Engineering and the Built Environment PhD or Professional Doctorate in Science and Engineering . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules Our Mechanical Engineering MSc aims to comprehensively develop your skillset to make you a well rounded and inherently employable professional engineer. Dr Peter Marshall Build on your engineering expertise and develop the skills to lead innovative solutions. You’ll further your understanding of advanced engineering design and analysis techniques, modern materials and their structural integrity, and contemporary manufacturing technology. Through practical, collaborative learning, you'll strengthen your problem-solving, critical, analytical, interpersonal, and computational skills. You'll also consider environmental and ethical factors, and develop your team working, leadership and management capabilities. You’ll complete your Master’s with your Major Project – a substantial research project on a relevant topic of your choice. What will I study? MSc Professional Experience 2 years part-time MSc Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Sustainable Environmental Design and Engineering Management Systems (15 credits) Engineering Quality Management (15 credits) Innovative Product Design and Manufacture (30 credits) Advanced Computer Aided Engineering (15 credits) Advanced Materials and Structural Integrity (15 credits) Computational Fluid Dynamics (15 credits) Automation and Robotics (15 credits) Engineering Major Project (60 credits) Into ARU Module details Professional Experience You can choose to study with us over two years (full-time), and take Professional Experience modules in Year 2, with a Preparation for Professional Experience module in Year 1. You'll complete your Postgraduate Major Project in Year 2. Professional experience modules Engineering Major Project (60 credits) Professional Project 1 (EBE) (60 credits) * Professional Project 2 (EBE) (60 credits) * Professional Placement 1 (60 credits) * Professional Placement 2 (60 credits) * Module details 2 years part-time It's possible to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as MSc/MA students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example if the MSc/MA course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. What are Professional Experience modules? Professional Experience modules are a great way to learn more about an industry. They take place in Year 2 of your course, with each module lasting approximately 12 weeks (or one trimester). You can choose which modules to take. Options include project work on campus, and industry placements. Our Placements Team is here to help you secure a placement. How is Mechanical Engineering assessed? You’ll be assessed in a variety of ways, including presentations, examinations, technical written reports and essays, team projects and coursework. Who teaches Mechanical Engineering at ARU? Read profiles of teaching and research staff on this course. Dr Ahad Ramezanpour Associate Professor Professor Hassan Shirvani Director, Engineering and Tribology Research Group Dr Shabnam Sadeghi Esfahlani Associate Professor in Robotics Dr Peter Marshall Senior Lecturer in Mechanical Engineering Dr Mohamed Yehia Senior Lecturer Dr Samuel J. McMaster Senior Lecturer Facilities You'll have the opportunity to use specialist equipment , including: CAD/CAM in our extensive engineering computer modelling centre 3D printers for rapid prototyping industrial-scale CNC milling machine, lathes and welding equipment electronic testing and measuring equipment tensile and compressive testing machines metal and plastic rapid prototyping machines hardness testing equipment. You can also make full use of other facilities including extensive library and IT resources, and get support with careers and employability , study skills , health and wellbeing , and more. Take a guided tour and meet our students . Speakers, societies and events We work closely with local IMechE, IET, and Chelmsford Science and Engineering Society to organise events. They're a great chance to hear about new technologies from expert speakers. There's also an active Engineering Society which runs events, and where you can meet like passionate and like-minded peers. The fee for Professional Experience modules is: £4,600 (2027-28) Part-time fees Part-time course fees assume that you’re studying at half the rate of a full-time student (50% intensity). Postgraduate MSc Mental Health Explore an issue that affects one in four people during their lifetime – and enhance your knowledge and understanding of mental health care. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Previous Section Course Overview Next Section Jump to a section Course overview Careers Teaching and modules Facilities Entry requirements Fees and funding Apply Apply now Book on a postgraduate open event MSc Part-time option(s) MSc Start date September 2027 January 2027 Location Distance learning Award MSc Duration 1 year full-time Part-time option(s) Start date September 2027 January 2027 Location Distance learning Award MSc Duration 2 years part-time 1st in the region for postgraduates progressing into senior roles. Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 Mental health problems affect people from all walks of life, with an impact felt by individuals, families and the wider community. This course lets you learn about mental health issues in an engaging and innovative way. You’ll explore the ‘craft of caring’ for people with a serious mental illness, and specialisms such as child and adolescent mental health, dementia care, and depression. You don’t need to be working in health care to apply. We welcome applicants who have a degree-level qualification and a passion for mental health. Take a guided tour and meet our students . Dr Julie Teatheredge explains how this MSc can help spread knowledge and understanding of mental health issues and how they affect the modern world. Close full-screen gallery. Dr Julie Teatheredge explains how this MSc can promote knowledge and understanding of mental health - and how mental health issues affects the modern world. Why ARU? Build your understanding of mental health issues Explore specialisms such as child and adolescent mental health care Study full- or part-time by distance learning Enhance your career options by achieving a postgraduate qualification Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers Strengthen your employment opportunities in health and social care. Your strong understanding of mental health issues will prepare you for middle or senior-ranking posts in the UK and internationally. You’ll also find that employers value your critical thinking and analytical skills. While the course covers innovation, research and leadership in mental health care it doesn’t lead to professional qualification as a mental health nurse. If you’re interested in nursing, please see our Nursing (Mental Health) degree . What can you do with an MSc Mental Health degree? You’ll graduate with the skills and knowledge for a career in a range of sectors. These include, for example, schools, charities and industry, and public and private health and social care services. Roles may include mental health lead, advisor, ambassador, or research assistant. Graduation doesn’t have to be the end of your time with us. You could choose to continue your academic career with a PhD programme at ARU . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules Explore aspects of contemporary, specialist and collaborative mental health care. Drawing on examples of good practice globally, you’ll develop your understanding of how collaborative working supports the delivery of high-quality mental health care. You’ll explore roles and responsibilities, and how services users and their families or carers are included in decision-making. You’ll also examine current issues in mental health, including the way mental illness is represented in the news, social media and in fictional sources such as films. Finally, you’ll complete a Major Project. This is a research or work-based project where you’ll explore a topic of your choice in detail. What will I study? MSc Part-time option(s) MSc Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Collaborative Mental Health Care Specialist Mental Health Care (30 credits) Contemporary Issues in Mental Health Care (30 credits) Into ARU Research Methodology (30 credits) Major Project Module details Part-time option(s) You can choose to study with us over two years (full-time), and take Professional Experience modules in Year 2, with a Preparation for Professional Experience module in Year 1. Year 1 Specialist Mental Health Care (30 credits) Promoting Innovation in Mental Health Care (30 credits) Contemporary Issues in Mental Health Care (30 credits) Into ARU Year 2 Research Methodology (30 credits) Major Project (60 credits) Module details How is MSc Mental Health assessed? We'll assess your progress in a number of ways, including assignments, presentations, a research proposal and Major Project, and a magazine article and portfolio. Facilities Enjoy a range of facilities designed to support your studies and career development. These include extensive library and IT resources, and careers support through our Employability Service . After you graduate, you’ll have lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Jump to a section Introduction Course options Key facts Student experience Teaching and assessment Entry requirements Fees and paying for university Facilities and showcase Accreditation Lecturers Careers Introduction Qualify to work as a music therapist in the UK and overseas on this accredited Masters degree in music therapy. Study in a centre of world-leading research and gain experience on clinical placements. Find out more about our impact ARU Music Therapy Impact ARU's Cambridge Institute for Music Therapy Research (CIMTR) has had a major impact both nationally and internationally, and in 2021 it was awarded a Queen's Anniversary Prize. Scholarships available: you may be eligible for our Alumni Scholarship or Music Therapy Entry Bursary to support your training. We have been training music therapists for over 30 years and were the first UK university to establish a music therapy Masters degree. We work closely with colleagues at the internationally renowned Cambridge Institute for Music Therapy Research . We earned the Queen's Anniversary Prize in 2021 for our music therapy research, receiving particular recognition for our focus on the wellbeing of people living with dementia. We welcome applications from people with relevant musical skills and appropriate clinical experience. Supported by experts, you’ll gain a strong foundation in the principles and practice of music therapy, underpinned by the latest research and evidence base. Our MA Music Therapy is accredited by the Health and Care Professions Council, so when you graduate you’ll be eligible to register with the HCPC – a legal requirement for your future career as a practising music therapist in the UK. Read more Teaching times 2025-26 (subject to change for 2026-27) Year 1: Mondays 9am-4pm Tuesdays 9am-6.30pm Wednesdays 9am-4pm (Tri 1 only) Placement two days a week (some weeks only) Year 2: Mondays 9am-6.30pm Placement one to two days a week Indicative teaching times for part-time course Year 1: Two teaching days per week Year 2: One teaching day per week Placement one to two days a week Year 3: One teaching day per week Placement one to two days a week Studying our two year full-time or three year part-time Masters in Music Therapy will show you how you can use your musical skills to support the health and well-being of patients and clients. We’ll introduce you to the most recent, effective music therapy approaches, which you can try out in clinical placements in locations such as schools, hospitals and other community settings. You’ll be supervised by qualified music therapists, gaining invaluable experience of working in a multidisciplinary team and preparation for your future career. At ARU, you’ll be taught in our purpose-designed music therapy centre and have access to a wide range of musical instruments, recording equipment and suite of computer music studios. Our experiential teaching includes developing your improvisation skills, focused work on your first instrument, and using keyboard, single line instrument and voice. You’ll also study music therapy theory and links to practice. You’ll have the opportunity to enrich your learning by working alongside our MA Dramatherapy students on some shared modules. There are just 15 places available on our Masters in Music Therapy, so you’ll learn as part of a small group and benefit from valuable placement opportunities. Places are filled in order of acceptance after which, if your application is successful, you will be offered a place on a waiting list. Places for our new part-time offer are very limited so we advise you to apply by 24 February 2027. The impact of our Music, Drama, Dance, Performing Arts, Film and Screen Studies research was judged as "world-leading" in the Research Excellence Framework 2021 (REF2021) . See photos of our anniversary event and our Storymap, showing alumni across the globe. Visit our MA Therapies anniversary page ARU Spotlight Amanda Lee After graduating, Amanda returned to her home country of Taiwan to work as a freelance music therapist and raise awareness of the discipline. Amanda's story Watch our video about MELODIC MELODIC: Music therapy Embedded in the Life Of Dementia Inpatient Care MELODIC is an ARU study investigating how music therapy can reduce distress on NHS inpatient wards for people with dementia. Find out more about MELODIC ARU Spotlight Caterina and Ana Read about MA Music Therapy student Caterina's experience at Hollanden Park Hospital with supervisor Ana. Read Cat and Ana's Spotlight interview Hear Sreeraj's story "The tutors were the pioneers in Music Therapy" Sreeraj now works as a Music Therapist with the NHS after completing our Masters. Find out how the course helped him. ARU Spotlight podcast Music Therapy placement special MA Music Therapy student Caterina and her placement supervisor Ana talk about how Caterina's placement at Hollanden Park Hospital inspired her Major Project. Listen to our podcast with Cat and Ana ARU Spotlight Rachael Stalker Rachael graduated from our MA Music Therapy in 2022, and now works as a music therapist at a Special Needs School. Find out how her placements on the course prepared her for work. Find out more about Rachael's experience ARU spotlight Jamal Glynn Jamal graduated in 2011 as the first MA music therapist in the world to use the steelpan as primary instrument. After this, he returned home to Trinidad, and within three weeks was assigned to the Ministry of Health. Read more about Jamal's experience ARU spotlight Rosie Axon After graduating from our MA Music Therapy, Rosie became Founder and Director at Chiltern Music Therapy, a not-for-profit organisation that provides music therapy to people of all ages across the UK. Fees and paying for university Facilities and showcase Specialist facilities and support As a postgraduate Music Therapy student at ARU you’ll: work in our purpose-built therapy centre, used for professional therapy consultations get support from our team of renowned music therapists learn from experts about the implications of the latest neuroscience research on therapy practice find out about our world-leading research work, including international projects such as Homeside . Take a guided tour and meet our students Hands-on learning There’s nothing like first-hand experience. Here at ARU, you’ll take part in clinical placements under the supervision of qualified therapists. Placements vary, and you could find yourself working in community settings, schools, hospitals or hospices. It’s great preparation for your future career. Take a closer look Our Creative Showcase shines a spotlight on what makes ARU creative and cultural – our spaces, places and people. Find out more about our community, the difference we make, the stories we tell, and the things that inspire us. You can also explore the work of our graduating students in our digital graduate showcase. Accreditation Health & Care Professions Council Our MA Music Therapy is accredited by the Health & Care Professions Council, allowing you to register with the HCPC when you graduate and work as a professional music therapist. Lecturers Previous. Next. Claire Molyneux Senior Lecturer Claire Molyneux's profile page [email protected] Alexandra Georgaki Senior Lecturer Alexandra Georgaki's profile page Connect with Alexandra on LinkedIn [email protected] Ellie Ruddock Lecturer Practitioner Ellie Ruddock's profile page Connect with Ellie on LinkedIn [email protected] Stavroulla Demetriou Senior Lecturer Stavroulla Demetriou's profile page [email protected] Rosie Sweet Lecturer Rosie Sweet's profile page [email protected] Careers When you graduate, you will be eligible to register with the Health and Care Professions Council. Registration is a legal requirement for practising music therapists in the UK and valued increasingly in other countries. As a qualified music therapist you’ll be able to work in the NHS, hospices, social services, education and the voluntary sector. You can also work privately or as a freelance with clients including adults and children with learning difficulties, mental health needs, or with communities such as refugees or the homeless. ARU’s links with the British Association for Music Therapy and our International Research Consortium will help you make contacts and gain employment and research opportunities. Over 30 years we've trained hundreds of therapists. They've gone on to train others and ARU alumni practice Music Therapy around the world. This StoryMap showcases the great work of 17 dramatherapy alumni and 47 music therapy alumni. Graduation doesn’t have to be the end of your time with us. You could choose to continue your academic career with a research programme at ARU, such as our PhD Music Therapy or PhD Dramatherapy . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. You might also be interested in our CPD Course Collaborative Music Practice in Health Care. These prizes are the highest national honour in higher and further education. They recognise outstanding work that shows the highest levels of quality and innovation and delivers significant public benefit. During this Masters in Music Therapy you’ll undertake at least two clinical placements.

In Year 1, your first placement will take place in one clinical area. An on-campus supervision group will support you as you develop your skills using critical reflection, experiential techniques and analytic writing about your process and casework.

Alongside your work placements you’ll explore the theoretical framework for the clinical knowledge and understanding of music therapy. You’ll also examine your role and identity as a trainee music therapist.

You’ll learn clinical improvisation skills in small groups, focusing on your main instrument, keyboard, voice and single-line instrument as well as taking workshops on group techniques.

Our training is framed by psychodynamic, developmental and neuroscience approaches to music therapy, but you will also learn about other models. You’ll have the opportunity to integrate what you’ve learned with your existing skills to develop your own effective approaches to clinical practice.

Modules are subject to change and availability.

You'll be assessed through a range of methods, including case presentations, demonstrating improvisation skills, written work including essays and a major project, and clinical portfolios.

","CoreModules":[{"Title":"Clinical Placements and Experiential Development 1","Description":"This module includes clinical experience (an introductory placement (minimum of four weeks) and a clinical placement (minimum of 12 weeks) in the workplace, and experiential development for students where you will develop reflexive skills and learn how to practise as a music therapist/dramatherapist. You'll gain a comprehensive understanding of music therapy/dramatherapy techniques and approaches for assessment, treatment and evaluation and how to apply these ethically in the clinical setting. This module aims to facilitate your individual development towards becoming a music therapist/dramatherapist, using critical reflection, experiential techniques in the experiential group, reflective analytic writing about your own process, and of your own case work. On successful completion of this module, you'll be able to demonstrate effective and collaborative work with service users and other professionals, clinical judgement, autonomous initiative and understanding of intersubjectivity in complex situations. You'll demonstrate a reflective critical awareness of the therapeutic alliance, and of how music therapy/dramatherapy has benefited the people you have worked with. As the placement experience is highly individual, this module is tailored to support you to act on feedback and university study on your journey towards becoming a qualified music therapist/dramatherapist.","Code":"MOD000631","HideMdfLink":false,"MdfLinkText":"View the full module definition","Id":"0f737043-b9b6-48a3-91fa-9bf36cf8c99e"},{"Title":"Music Therapy and Dramatherapy Multidisciplinary Theoretical Studies","Description":"On this module, you will discover the theoretical framework for the clinical knowledge and understanding of music therapy/dramatherapy, together with your role in securing, maintaining and improving health and well-being for patients/clients. Through lectures and seminars, you will develop an informed understanding of core processes in therapeutic practice (e.g. the therapeutic frame, the centrality of the therapeutic relationship, transference, and counter-transference). In your second year studying MA Music Therapy you’ll take on more advanced clinical work, learning how to practise as a music therapist without discrimination.

Under placement supervisors, you’ll work independently and show an advanced level of evaluative clinical knowledge and skills.

Your work placements will either be in two different clinical areas, or one six-month placement in the same setting. You’ll show you understand fully the assessment and referral processes relating to casework and be able to work in a multidisciplinary team in community-based and other settings.

You’ll explore ethical considerations and issues of cultural diversity and practice, using evaluation methods as preparation for your own research.

The MA Therapies Major Project will involve some clinical or theoretical evaluation and research. You’ll receive a basic introduction to research methodology and be supported by specialists in clinical and theoretical aspects of psychological therapies. You’ll also have access to research resources both nationally and internationally.

Modules are subject to change and availability.

You'll be assessed through a range of methods, including case presentations, demonstrating improvisation skills, written work including essays and a major project, and clinical portfolios.

Main
  • Usually an honours degree classification (or equivalent) in music or a related discipline such as psychology, teaching, nursing, social work.
  • A high standard of sensitive, flexible and communicative musicianship demonstrated on at least one instrument (including voice). Keyboard or other accompanying instrument (eg guitar) skills are also required. Musical skills are assessed at shortlisting and interview stage.
  • A sustained period (one year or equivalent) of relevant experience with people with additional needs. For example, work/voluntary experience in learning disability, mental health or hospital settings with both children and adults, preferably undertaken following completion of undergraduate studies. Appropriate motivational and emotional maturity. Ability to reflect on self in relation to others. An understanding and knowledge of the music therapy field. Good written and verbal communication skills.
  • If English is not your first language you will be expected to demonstrate a certificated level of proficiency of at least IELTS 7.0 (Academic level with no individual score being lower than 6.5) or equivalent English Language qualification as recognised by Anglia Ruskin University. It is strongly recommended that applicants do not attend for interview until they are approaching this score, as this may adversely affect their ability to participate fully in the interview procedures. 

To receive an offer of a place on this course you must be successful at interview.

An Enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) disclosure will also be required. You will also be required to register with the Online Update Service.

A satisfactory Occupational Health clearance will also be required.

Two satisfactory references are required. These should be from relevant clinical experience (paid employment or voluntary) and/or academic if recent graduate and/or other professional.

As part of the shortlisting process you will be required to supply a music portfolio video.

Interview and audition

As this is a professional therapy training, we'll ask you to attend a workshop, interview and audition if you're shortlisted.

These are group workshops. If we do not have sufficient interviews booked for a session we may need to rearrange your interview and audition. We recommend you do not book travel or accommodation until one week before your interview.

Find out more about our Music Therapy portfolio, interview and audition requirements.

Music Therapy bursaries

We offer a number of bursaries to MA Music Therapy students. They support some of the activities you'll undertake as part of your training.

Music Therapy Entry Bursary: apply in your first year (see full details). Worth up to £1,000.

Music Therapy Placement Travel and Clinical Supervision Bursary: apply in your final year (we'll invite applications). Worth up to £300.

The Alice Zeitlyn Music Therapy Bursary: apply in your final year (we'll invite applications). Usually worth between £100 – £250.

Postgraduate Music Therapy MPhil, PhD Research ( full-time, part-time) Cambridge January 2027, April, September 2027 This course is located in the Cambridge Institute of Music Therapy Research . Distance-learning supervision available. Apply online For application deadlines visit our how to apply page . Overview Our Cambridge Institute for Music Therapy Research (CIMTR) is an international centre for research into music therapy, putting you at the heart of new music therapy research worldwide. Our large community of PhD students, and links to seven other universities across the world, will make you part of a team that leads on music therapy research. Full description CIMTR leads music therapy research for adults, older people, young people and children with a range of issues. We specialise in finding out what works clinically in music therapy and how it works, including which theoretical frameworks such as neurology, psychology, psychotherapy, psychoanalysis best inform the work. Our researchers are involved in public policy, and we regularly provide talks for parliament, keynotes around the world at international conferences. Our supervisory team supports full and part-time doctoral students, including self-funded projects , and projects funded from the University (such as Vice Chancellor's Scholarships ) or funded by external organisations. Full-time PhD projects are completed in 3-4 years, while part-time projects are usually completed within 5-6 years. Projects may be independent research or embedded within larger externally funded research studies. Supervisory teams have expertise in your chosen field or area of research and will support you through all stages of study design, ethics application, data collection, analysis, and write-up. You'll meet at least monthly with their supervisors if full-time, or bi-monthly if part-time, although the frequency of meetings may vary based on individual needs and study complexity along your doctoral journey. All meetings, actions, and research progress are recorded on the ARU Doctoral School ’s online platform. You'll be supported by their supervisors and the Doctoral School to complete mandatory, as well as optional training courses. Your supervisors will support you to complete required milestones throughout the programme. CIMTR is based in the state-of-the-art Jerome Booth Music Therapy Centre, including a research laboratory where practical music therapy and music and brain research can be undertaken in purpose-built spaces. Here, you'll benefit from engaging with the wider CIMTR team, which serves as a part of their learning community. You'll also have access to the extensive facilities offered by Cambridge School of Art, including a recital hall, a suite of computer music studios and music practice rooms, a fully-equipped drama studio, and two large drama rehearsal spaces. The institute coordinates PhD seminar days twice a year in Cambridge with the option of online attendance. This is an important opportunity for you to present your current stage of work, bring dilemmas and questions for discussion, and learn from other students and supervisors. Social engagement opportunities are integral to PhD days and create a collaborative learning community. Workshops are also offered as part of the seminars on topics such as academic publishing; analysis; research frameworks, ethics applications, and more. You'll be encouraged to join a monthly meeting with the whole CIMTR team. This provides an opportunity to present work or to bring questions to the wider team for discussion. We host a free monthly webinar series that invites internationally renowned researchers to share their research related to music therapy, arts therapies and music interventions. As a doctoral student, you can assist in organising and facilitating this series during one academic year. This offers experience in planning and coordinating events and provides the opportunity to meet a wide range of academics from around the world. Find out more about our supervisors, areas of supervision, and current PhD researchers on our doctoral programme page . Completion times MPhil: full-time 1-3 years, part-time 2-4 years. PhD via progression from MPhil, including that period: full-time 2.5-5 years, part-time 3.5-6 years. PhD: full-time 2-4 years, part-time 3-6 years. For further guidance on the duration of research degrees please refer to the Research Degrees Regulations . Music therapy PhD project opportunities World-leading research at ARU The Queen's Anniversary Prize For our music therapy work Our neurorehabilitation clinic As seen on BBC News CIMTR doctoral programme Supervision and support Visit the CIMTR doctoral programme page to find out about our available supervisors and areas of supervision, as well as our current PhD research. Where you'll research Your faculty In the Faculty of Arts, Humanities, Education and Social Sciences, we use our expertise and connections in Cambridge and beyond to nurture creativity through experimentation and risk-taking, and encourage critical thinking, in order to educate, entertain, inspire and understand, as well as to improve people’s lives. Visit your faculty Where can I study? Cambridge Our campus is close to the centre of Cambridge, often described as the perfect student city. Explore our Cambridge campus Fees & funding Course fees UK students, 2026/27 (per year) £5,238 UK students, 2026/27 (part-time, per year) £2,619 International students, 2026/27 (per year) £17,500 International students, 2026/27 (part-time, per year) £8,750 Bench fees In some cases extra costs known as bench fees will be charged for a postgraduate research degree. These are to cover additional/exceptional costs directly related to a specific research project. Some examples of these costs are (the list is not exhaustive): equipment hire, access costs to specialist equipment/workshops, volunteer expenses, specialist tissue/cell culture, specialist reagents or materials, specialist software, access to specialist databases, data collection costs, specialist media, recording or digital storage needs. We charge bench fees in bands. They may apply for every year of your course. These bands are the same for full- and part-time students. If you have to pay bench fees this will be made clear at your interview, and stated in your offer letter. For 2026/27 the bench fee bands are: £500 £1,400 £2,400 £4,900 £9,800 PhD by Published Work Initial registration: £1,700 Full registration: £4,900 Writing up fees 2026/27 £1,400 How do I pay my fees? You can pay your fees upfront, in full or in instalments – though you won't need to pay until you've accepted an offer to study with us. Find out more about paying your fees . Funding For advice on the Doctoral Loan and other sources of funding, including ARU scholarships, visit our finance guide for postgraduate researchers . You might also find The Alternative Guide to Postgraduate Funding helpful. ARU research ARU's academic excellence was recognised in 2021, as part of the Research Excellence Framework (REF), an exercise which assesses the quality of academic research. Sixteen areas of our work were classed as generating world-leading research . The results showed that we're making a significant impact on the societies we live in. Careers We will provide you with many opportunities for career development and training, in areas like writing up a paper for publication; placing an academic article; giving a conference paper; the doctoral writing style; updates on research methods and literature searches; internet training; editing skills for doctoral research; subsequent monograph publication; and dealing with festivals, agents, and publishers. You might also be able to take on teaching responsibilities in the department, or organise research events like seminars and conferences. In conjunction with the University’s research support, you can request specific support for writing-up, conference papers, general research methods and other research skills if you need it. You can also take part in running research projects where appropriate and link your research ideas accordingly. Contact details If you're interested in finding out more about research study opportunities in this area, please email [email protected] We recommended that you also contact one of the above potential supervisors before applying to discuss your plans, particularly if you do not have a degree in music therapy. Entry requirements MPhil or PhD with progression from MPhil: You’ll need a Bachelors degree or equivalent with first or upper second class honours, in a related subject area. PhD: You’ll need a Masters degree or equivalent in a related subject area. Please note we consider candidates for PhD with progression from MPhil in the first instance. If you want to be considered for direct entry to the PhD route then this can be discussed at interview if you are shortlisted. Please note you’ll also need to provide academic justification for this request. If English is not your first language, you'll require a minimum IELTS score of 6.5, with a minimum of 5.5 in each component (or equivalent test). If you don't meet our English language requirements, we offer a range of courses which could help you achieve the level required for entry. Loading... Entry requirements are not currently available, please try again later. Important additional notes Our published entry requirements are a guide only and our decision will be based on your overall suitability for the programme as well as whether you meet the minimum entry requirements. Contact our postgraduate research degree team for more information about studying a PhD, MPhil or Professional Doctorate at ARU. You'll need a computer and reliable internet access to successfully engage with your research programme. Postgraduate MSc Project Management Develop the expertise to plan and deliver complex projects across any industry with our Association for Project Management accredited degree. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Previous Section Course Overview Next Section Jump to a section Course overview Careers Teaching and modules Facilities Entry requirements Fees and funding Apply Apply now Book on a postgraduate open event MSc 2 years part-time Distance learning MSc Start date September 2027 January 2027 May 2027 Location Chelmsford Award MSc Duration 1 year full-time You can choose to start this course in September, January or May. Course durations may vary slightly and you can contact us for more information. Course content and modules remain the same. 2 years part-time You can choose to study this course part-time, and start in September or January. The course durations vary slightly: 2 years (September starts) or 28 months (January starts). Course content and modules remain the same. Distance learning You can study this course part-time over 2-3 years, starting in September, January or May. The course durations vary slightly but course content and modules remain the same. 1st in the region for postgraduates progressing into senior roles. Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 Our Master's degree takes a distinctive, people-focused approach to project management. Every manager brings their own strengths, experience and perspective – and you’ll develop the skills and confidence to lead projects in your own way. You'll also gain a comprehensive understanding of the project management process, informed by established management principles. You'll have the opportunity to put your skills into practice with SHoKE (Students at the Heart of Knowledge Exchange) . And you can join any of the three research groups in our School of Engineering and the Built Environment : Built Environment Futures; Engineering, System, Design and Transformation; and Sustainably Resilient Infrastructure and Communities. Accreditation Our course is accredited by the Association for Project Management (APM), meaning you’ll have access to their resources, communities of learning, and communities of practice. From ARU to MBE: Charlotte's postgraduate journey in project management. Close full-screen gallery. From ARU to MBE: Charlotte's postgraduate journey in project management. Why ARU? Connect with industry professionals through our relationships with APM, RICS and CIOB Enjoy free student membership of the APM and discounts on industry events Explore the role of a project manager, as well as management processes Study an accredited course which gives you access to specialist resources Study your way, with full-time, part-time or distance learning options Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers The MSc equipped me with the knowledge, confidence, and strategic perspective to successfully lead major transformation initiatives in a fast-paced NHS environment. Ajay Sooknah, Princess Alexandra Hospital NHS Trust Graduate ready to make an impact, whether you’re developing new products, implementing technology, managing major infrastructure or driving business transformation. Your project management skills can open doors to roles in a range of industries. These include business and professional services, construction, manufacturing, finance, technology, defence and aerospace. You could pursue a career as a project manager or move into wider management roles, helping organisations deliver complex projects, improve performance and lead organisational change. What can you do with a Project Management degree? Graduates from this course have successfully become: Assistant Project Manager Associate Project Director Business or Systems Analyst Change Manager Consultant Project Administrator Contracts Manager Head of Projects/Programmes PMO Director/Manager/Officer Project Controls Manager Project Coordinator Project Engineer Project Planner Project/Programme/Portfolio Director Project/Programme/Portfolio Manager Project/Programme Office Support Graduation doesn’t have to be the end of your time with us. You could choose to continue your academic career with a research programme at ARU, such as our PhD Engineering and the Built Environment or Professional Doctorate in Business and Management . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules Engaging lectures with interactive activities, tutorials and discussions, enhance your learning experience in a diverse environment. Hussein Adebayo Ibrahim, Course Director Develop the knowledge, practical skills and critical thinking to manage projects in range of organisations and industries. Our teaching combines project management theory, current research and practical application, helping you make informed decisions when tackling real-world challenges. You’ll learn from academic experts, industry practitioners, and professional bodies including APM and CIOB . Guest lectures give you valuable insights into current practice, emerging challenges and the skills employers value. What will I study? MSc 2 years part-time Distance learning MSc Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Project Management Systems (15 credits) Management Theory (15 credits) Project Management Techniques (15 credits) Project Planning and Control (15 credits) Research Design and Methods (15 credits) Project Management Context (15 credits) Management Practice (15 credits) Cost and Financial Management (15 credits) Dissertation (60 credits) Into ARU Module details 2 years part-time It's possible to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as MSc/MA students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example if the MSc/MA course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. Distance learning There'll be times when you'll study two modules simultaneously during a trimester. Our tutors will help you to manage your workload and assessment deadlines. Please contact us to discuss the pacing of this course and the options available to you. Email [email protected] or call 01245 686707. Find out more about this course on our Distance Learning website . Free student membership with the Association for Project Management Membership includes lots of useful online resources and access to the Project Journal archive to aid your studies as well as discounted access to APM events , which are great opportunities to learn, meet influential figures and explore new ways of thinking and working. How is Project Management assessed? You’ll be assessed in a number of different ways including research projects and reports, written coursework including essays and case studies, group work and presentations, examinations and a dissertation. Who teaches Project Management at ARU? Read profiles of teaching and research staff on this course. Dr Hussein Adebayo Ibrahim Senior Lecturer Dr Federica Pascale Associate Professor Dr Christian Henjewele Senior Lecturer Dr Richard Brett Deputy Head of School Falilat Giwa Lecturer Dr Olalekan Oshodi Lecturer Facilities Enjoy a range of facilities designed to support your studies and career development. These include extensive library and IT resources, and careers support through our Employability Service . After you graduate, you’ll have lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . You can also access support, should you need it, with study skills, health and wellbeing, and more. Take a guided tour and meet our students . Please enable JavaScript for "Fees Information" section to function. Other equivalent qualifications may be accepted for entry to this course; please email [email protected] for further information. Applicants to undergraduate courses can also check our information about undergraduate entry qualifications . You'll need a computer and reliable internet access to successfully engage with your course. 2 years part-time See entry requirements for the MA or MSc Distance learning See entry requirements for the MA or MSc International students We welcome applications from international and EU students, and accept a range of international qualifications.
